- 基础检查和可用环境下的 JIT compile/correctness 验证通过。

title: Balance dsv4 sparse-attn proj_b dequant across both AIV cores
body:
## Summary
- The `proj_b` INT8 GEMM + dequant in `models/deepseek/v4/decode_sparse_attn.py` is a fused cube+vector (1c2v) `pl.spmd` block. With the default `SplitMode.NONE` the cube->vector handoff emits `tpush_to_aiv {split = 0}` and the AIV kernel degenerates into `if subblock_idx == 0 / else`: vector lane 0 runs the whole epilogue and holds the only `tstore`, while lane 1 is a phantom (`valid_row=0/valid_col=0`, no compute, no store) that only does the `tpop` handshake. The stage is effectively 1c1v — only one vector core does useful work.
- Because lane 1 just waits on the cube's pushes, its duration ~= the AIC duration; lane 0's duration = max(cube feed time, its own vec+store time). `proj_b` is **vector-bound** (epilogue vec+store >> cube feed), so lane 0 >> lane 1 and the two AIV cores look badly imbalanced. A cube-bound stage like `proj_a` keeps lane 0 ~= lane 1 ~= AIC, so its idle second core is harmless and the same degeneration is invisible — this is a property of the workload balance, not a difference in epilogue op count (both are 4x `[32,128]`).
- On-device (`a2a3`) `proj_b_aiv` before: lane0 mean ~137us vs lane1 mean ~39us, peak 199us.
- Fix: add `optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.LEFT_RIGHT)]` to the `proj_b` spmd block so the handoff becomes `split = 1` and the `subblock_idx` branch is removed — the block is column-halved and each AIV subblock post-processes `B_N_TILE/2` output channels (with its own slice of the per-channel `wo_b_scale`) and emits a real `tstore`.
- After: both lanes do equal work (~106us each), peak drops to ~159us (-20%), and the `proj_b` region wall-clock falls 225.7us -> 192.9us (-14.5%). `attn_out` matches golden on `a2a3`.
- `LEFT_RIGHT` (channel split) is used rather than `UP_DOWN` (row/T split): in this kernel `UP_DOWN` mis-lowers the loop-invariant `[1, B_N_TILE]` `wo_b_scale` broadcast (the tile feeding `TCOLEXPANDMUL` is allocated but never loaded), producing incorrect output (golden mismatch). `LEFT_RIGHT` keeps the per-channel scale correct and passes.

## Related Issues
Related to #531 — that issue diagnoses the same `split = 0` 1c1v degeneration in fused 1c2v stages and additionally requests a swimlane/DFX change (distinguish idle/sync-only time from compute time). This PR applies only the kernel-side fix for `proj_b`; it does not change the swimlane, so it does not close the issue.

title: [Bug] Swimlane: the two vector subblocks of a fused 1c2v show very unequal durations
body:
### Diagnosis

**simpler** (DFX / merged swimlane) — the swimlane timeline does not distinguish idle/sync-only time from compute time, so a phantom (idle-waiting) vector subblock is drawn with a substantial duration.

### Description

**Main question: in a fused 1c2v stage, the two vector subblocks (2v) report very unequal durations in the merged swimlane — one is up to ~3x the other — which looks wrong for a symmetric 1c2v.**

Investigated on `models/deepseek/v4/decode_sparse_attn.py` and reproduced on a minimal standalone mix kernel (one matmul -> vector epilogue -> store). Measured per-stage means (each stage is a fused cube->vector region):

| stage | AIC | AIV subblock0 (even core) | AIV subblock1 (odd core) |
|---|---|---|---|
| proj_a | 47.3 | 48.1 | 47.0 |
| proj_b | 48.4 | **129.5** | **45.0** |
| attn_out_scale (minimal repro) | 44.2 | **71.4** | **43.2** |

proj_b and the minimal repro show the two vector subblocks badly unequal; proj_a happens to look balanced.

**Root cause found.** The emitted ptoas shows the cube->vector handoff is `tpush_to_aiv {split = 0}`, and the AIV kernel is an `if subblock_idx == 0 / else`:
- **subblock 0** does all the real work and holds the only `tstore`.
- **subblock 1** is a phantom: its tiles are `valid_row=0 valid_col=0`, no compute and no `tstore`, only the `tpop_from_aic` handshake.

So every one of these stages is effectively **1c1v** — only one vector core works. Key relationship: **subblock 1's duration is approximately equal to the AIC duration** in all three stages (47~47, 45~48, 43~44), because the phantom subblock just waits on the cube's pushes and exits when the cube stops feeding. subblock 0's duration = `max(cube feed time, its own vec+store time)`.

This explains proj_a vs proj_b:
- **proj_a is cube-bound** (vec work <= cube time) -> subblock0 ~ subblock1 ~ AIC -> looks balanced (the idle 2nd core is harmless here).
- **proj_b / attn_out_scale are vector-bound** (subblock0 vec+store >> cube) -> subblock0 >> subblock1 (= AIC floor) -> looks unequal.

Confirmation it is the split=0 degeneration: adding `optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)]` to the minimal repro flips the handoff to `split = 1`, removes the `subblock_idx` branch, and both subblocks then process half the rows **with a real `tstore`** -> durations balance (44.7 vs 44.3, vs 71.4/43.2 before).

**The swimlane problem.** The phantom subblock 1 is drawn with a **substantial duration (approximately the AIC feed time)**, not near-zero. From the timeline alone you cannot tell that subblock 1 is **idle-waiting on `tpop`** rather than computing — it just looks like "the two vector cores took unequal time." This (a) makes a 1c1v-degenerate stage read as a merely-unbalanced 1c2v, and (b) hides that the second vector core is doing no useful work. The same ambiguity inflates the AIC bars: identical-workload cube tasks (fixed-size matmul) span ~3us to ~95us because the bar is wall-clock occupancy including dispatch + producer->consumer GM waits, not compute.

**Request:** in the swimlane, make idle/sync-only time (waiting on `tpop`/`tpush`, dispatch, GM-dependency stalls) visually distinct from compute time, so a phantom subblock and a stalled cube are not shown as if they were busy.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Run a fused 1c2v kernel with the swimlane enabled: `python models/deepseek/v4/decode_sparse_attn.py -d <dev> --enable-l2-swimlane`.
2. Open `dfx_outputs/merged_swimlane_*.json`, aggregate `proj_b_aiv` (and `proj_a_aiv`) durations by core parity (subblock 0 vs 1), and compare with `ptoas/proj_b.pto` (`tpush_to_aiv {split = 0}`, phantom else-branch).
3. Compare AIC mean vs subblock-1 mean per stage to see subblock1 ~ AIC.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `56c01e1d` |
| pypto | `533d629d` (branch: main) |
| simpler | `f1062ff0` |
| ptoas | (CI-pinned) |
| CANN | not detected |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Driver: 26.0.rc1. Screenshot and swimlane JSON to be attached by the reporter.

title: Perf: fuse DeepSeek-V4 hc_pre into a single SPMD scope
body:
## Summary

Fuses DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre` (`models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py`) from **5 separate `pl.spmd` scopes into 1**.

Previously `hc_pre` ran as `linear` → `split_pre_post` → `write_post` → `comb_sinkhorn` → `mix_x`, bridged through GM intermediates (`mixes`, `pre_val_store`, `post_pad_store`, `comb_logits`). Now all five fold into ONE spmd loop over the dynamic token tiles: per tile the RMS+linear matmul writes a `mixes_gm` scratch row and reads it straight back (intra-task) to produce `pre`/`post`/`mix_x`/`comb` directly — dropping the cross-scope GM intermediates and the per-scope dispatch overhead.

## Changes

- **Single fused scope.** `pre` is kept in Vec and consumed by `mix_x` in-scope (per-head `[TILE,1]` scales via transpose + materialize); `comb` groups are read 8-wide from the same `mixes_gm` row; `post`/`comb` stored per tile.
- **`D_TILE` 512 → 256.** In the fused scope the `mix_x` FP32 tiles share Vec UB with the matmul/sinkhorn buffers; 512 overflows the 192KB Vec limit.
- **Dynamic shape (`T_DYN`) preserved** — one compile serves decode and prefill.

## Performance

L2 swimlane on board (Ascend a2a3, decode, T=128), before (5 scopes) vs after (1 fused scope), **median of 3 runs** (per-run range in parens):

| Metric | Before (5 scopes) | After (1 fused) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Device span (end-to-end latency)** | **169.2 us** (165.7–170.9) | **134.9 us** (131.1–136.1) | **−20%** |
| Total busy (compute) | 1809 us | 1789 us | ≈ unchanged |
| — cube (matmul) busy | 463.5 us | 469.2 us | ≈ unchanged |
| — vector busy | 1338.8 us (across 5 funcs) | 1336.3 us (1 func) | ≈ unchanged |
| spmd scopes / sub-tasks | 5 / 56 | 1 / 24 | 5 → 1 |

The per-run span ranges do not overlap (before 166–171 us vs after 131–136 us), so the delta is robust. Compute (busy) is essentially identical — `D_TILE` 512→256 does **not** add work, the kernel body is the same — so the ~20% lower device span comes entirely from eliminating the inter-scope overhead (5 dispatches → 1, no cross-scope GM round-trips, per-tile epilogue overlapping the next tile's matmul).

## Dependencies

Requires the pypto codegen fixes that make a fused cube→vec kernel work:
- **#1761** — `SplitVectorKernel` `split=0` cube↔vec pipe ops replayed into both AIV subblocks (the 507018 deadlock when fusing cube+vec in one task).
- **#1768** — orchestration codegen hoists the injected dynamic GM pipe buffer above the `t_dim` it is sized by (the use-before-decl compile error for the dynamic case).

## Validation (on board, Ascend a2a3)

- `hc_pre.py` decode + prefill: `x_mixed` / `post` / `comb` PASS.
- Downstream importers that inline `hc_pre` (it is `@pl.jit.inline`) re-verified — no regression:
  - `decode_attention_csa.py` — `kv_cache` + `x_out` PASS (complex dynamic, single-device).
  - `moe_ep.py` — `x_next` PASS (distributed, 2-rank).

Remaining importers (`moe.py`, `prefill_attention_swa.py`, `prefill_attention_csa.py`) share the same inline pattern (lower risk; not yet re-verified).

title: perf(dsv4 decode_sparse_attn): batch qk_pv matmul to M=32 (-53% qk_pv core-time)
body:
## Summary

- Batch the `qk_pv` QK/PV cube matmuls to **M=32** (new `QK_M_TILE`): the shared sparse-KV tile is extracted L1→L0 once per 2 head-tiles (2× reuse) instead of once per `H_TILE=16` head-tile, and the head-tile loop is software-pipelined (`stage=2`). `qk_pv` was L1→L0-bound on the re-streamed KV tile.
- **Decoupled from storage/merge:** the `[32, …]` matmul/softmax result is sliced back into two `[16, …]` writes at bit-identical `sparse_blk_*` offsets, so `merge_norm` and the `sparse_blk_*` layout are unchanged and `attn_out` is bit-identical to the per-head-tile path.
- **Split-free:** the `[32,128]` softmax fits the 192 KB Vec budget without a cross-core split. (M=64 deferred — its `[64,128]` softmax and co-resident QK+PV L0C accumulators exceed the Vec/L0C budgets.)
- **Perf** (a2a3, L2 swimlane, `compress-ratio 4`, vs current `main`): qk_pv cube core-time **−52.9%**, vector core-time **−53.5%**, qk_pv wall-span **−50.9%**, whole-kernel AICore wall **−15.3%**.
- **Correctness:** bit-correct vs the torch golden (`ratio_allclose`), validated on device at `compress-ratio` 0 and 4.

## Related Issues

None.

title: DeepSeek V4 缺少与 model.py 对齐的 RoPE/YaRN real cos/sin table 生成逻辑
body:
## 背景

`model.py` 中的 DeepSeek attention 使用 `precompute_freqs_cis()` 生成 RoPE/YaRN 频率表：

- 先按 `rope_theta` / `compress_rope_theta`、`rope_factor`、`beta_fast`、`beta_slow`、`original_seq_len` 计算 YaRN 修正后的角频率。
- 再通过 `torch.polar(torch.ones_like(freqs), freqs)` 生成 complex `freqs_cis`。
- `apply_rotary_emb()` 通过 `torch.view_as_complex()`、complex multiply 和 `torch.view_as_real()` 对 interleaved even/odd rotary pairs 做 RoPE。
- `inverse=True` 时使用 `freqs_cis.conj()`，用于 attention output rope slice 的 de-rotation。

当前 `models/deepseek/v4` 路径下的实现不使用 complex tensor。各 PyPTO kernel 已经通过显式 real-valued `freqs_cos` / `freqs_sin` 输入完成 RoPE apply，但仓库里还缺少一个与 `model.py` 语义等价的 host-side RoPE/YaRN table 生成模块。目前多个 standalone fixture 使用类似 `torch.cos(torch.arange(...) * 1e-3)` / `torch.sin(torch.arange(...) * 1e-3)` 的 synthetic table，这不是 DeepSeek YaRN 频率表。

因此需要补齐的是：在 V4 路径上实现 `model.py::precompute_freqs_cis()` 等价的 real cos/sin table 生成逻辑，并统一各模块的 fixture/runtime 调用。

## 当前 DeepSeek V4 RoPE 接口和读取逻辑

### 1. 公共 Q/KV 投影

`models/deepseek/v4/qkv_proj_rope.py`

- `materialize_rope_rows(...)`
  - 输入 full table：
    - `freqs_cos: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_DIM], BF16`
    - `freqs_sin: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_DIM], BF16`
    - `position_ids: [T_DYN], INT32`
  - 输出 token-local table：
    - `rope_cos_t: [T_DYN, ROPE_DIM], BF16`
    - `rope_sin_t: [T_DYN, ROPE_DIM], BF16`
  - 只做按 position 取行，不做三角函数计算。

- `qkv_proj_rope(...)`
  - 输入 token-local table：
    - `rope_cos: [T_DYN, ROPE_DIM], BF16`
    - `rope_sin: [T_DYN, ROPE_DIM], BF16`
  - 对 Q head rope slice 和 KV rope slice 做正向 RoPE。
  - 内部通过 `j >> 1` duplicate gather cos/sin，通过 `j ^ 1` swap 和 sign mask 实现 interleaved pair rotation。

### 2. Decode attention 编排模块

`decode_attention_swa.py`

- `compress_ratio = 0`
- 接收 full table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
- 内部按 `position_ids[t]` materialize：
  - `rope_cos_t/rope_sin_t: [T, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
- `rope_cos_t/rope_sin_t` 同时传给：
  - `qkv_proj_rope(...)`：Q/KV 正向 RoPE
  - `decode_sparse_attn.sparse_attn(...)`：attention output rope slice 的 inverse RoPE

`decode_attention_csa.py`

- `compress_ratio = 4`
- 接收 full table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
- 内部派生：
  - `rope_cos_t/rope_sin_t: [T, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
  - `step_cos/step_sin: [B, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2], FP32`
  - `cmp_cos/cmp_sin: [B, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2], FP32`
- `rope_cos_t/rope_sin_t` 给 `qkv_proj_rope(...)` 和 `decode_sparse_attn.sparse_attn(...)`。
- `step_cos/step_sin` 给 `decode_indexer.indexer(...)`。
- `cmp_cos/cmp_sin` 给 `decode_compressor_ratio4.compressor_ratio4(...)`。

`decode_attention_hca.py`

- `compress_ratio = 128`
- 接收 full table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
- 内部派生：
  - `rope_cos_t/rope_sin_t: [T, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
  - `cmp_cos/cmp_sin: [B, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2], FP32`
- `rope_cos_t/rope_sin_t` 给 `qkv_proj_rope(...)` 和 `decode_sparse_attn.sparse_attn(...)`。
- `cmp_cos/cmp_sin` 给 `decode_compressor_ratio128.compressor_ratio128(...)`。

### 3. Decode 子模块

`decode_compressor_ratio4.py`

- 不接收 full table。
- 接收上层已 materialize 的 half table：
  - `cos: [B, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2], FP32`
  - `sin: [B, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2], FP32`
- 对 pooled KV rope slice 做正向 RoPE，写入 compressed KV cache。

`decode_compressor_ratio128.py`

- 与 ratio-4 decode compressor 类似：
  - `cos: [B_DYN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2], FP32`
  - `sin: [B_DYN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2], FP32`
- 用于 ratio-128 compressed KV 写入路径。

`decode_indexer.py`

- 接收 per-batch half table：
  - `cos: [B, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2], FP32`
  - `sin: [B, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2], FP32`
- 对 indexer query 的 rope slice 做正向 RoPE。
- 注意：如果 decode path 中 `S > 1`，当前 per-batch half table 设计可能会让同一 batch 内多个 token 复用同一行 cos/sin，需要和 `model.py` 的逐 token `freqs_cis[start_pos:start_pos+seqlen]` 语义单独核对。

`decode_indexer_compressor.py`

- 接收 per-batch half table：
  - `cos: [B, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2], FP32`
  - `sin: [B, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2], FP32`
- 对 inner compressed KV rope slice 做正向 RoPE。

`decode_sparse_attn.py`

- 接收 token-local table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [T, ROPE_DIM], BF16`
- 对 attention output rope slice 做 inverse RoPE。
- 复用同一组 cos/sin table，只在 apply 公式中使用 conjugate 对应的符号。

### 4. Prefill attention 编排模块

`prefill_attention_swa.py`

- `compress_ratio = 0`
- 接收 full table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
- 调用 `materialize_rope_rows(...)` 得到 token-local `rope_cos_t/rope_sin_t`。
- token-local table 传给 `qkv_proj_rope(...)` 和 `prefill_sparse_attn(...)`。

`prefill_attention_csa.py`

- `compress_ratio = 4`
- 接收 full table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
- 调用 `materialize_rope_rows(...)` 得到 token-local table。
- full table 继续传给：
  - `prefill_compressor_ratio4(...)`
  - `prefill_indexer(...)`
- 子模块内部按 compressed write position 取 half-width cos/sin。

`prefill_attention_hca.py`

- `compress_ratio = 128`
- 接收 full table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
- 调用 `materialize_rope_rows(...)` 得到 token-local table。
- full table 继续传给 `prefill_compressor_ratio128(...)`。

### 5. Prefill 子模块

`prefill_compressor_ratio4.py`

- 接收 full table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
- 对每个 compressed write token 计算：
  - `cmp_pos = write_pos + 1 - COMPRESS_RATIO`
- 读取 `freqs_cos/freqs_sin[cmp_pos, :ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2]`，对 pooled KV rope slice 做正向 RoPE。

`prefill_compressor_ratio128.py`

- 接收 full table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_DIM], BF16`
- 同样通过 `cmp_pos = write_pos + 1 - COMPRESS_RATIO` 读取 half-width cos/sin 行，对 ratio-128 pooled KV rope slice 做正向 RoPE。

`prefill_indexer.py`

- 接收 full table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
- 主要是编排模块，把 full table 继续传给 `prefill_indexer_compressor(...)`。

`prefill_indexer_compressor.py`

- 接收 full table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], BF16`
- 内部同样通过 `cmp_pos = write_pos + 1 - COMPRESS_RATIO` 读取 half-width cos/sin 行，对 inner compressed KV rope slice 做正向 RoPE。

`prefill_sparse_attn.py`

- 接收 token-local table：
  - `freqs_cos/freqs_sin: [T, ROPE_DIM], BF16`
- 对 attention output rope slice 做 inverse RoPE。

## 与 `model.py` 的公式对齐

`model.py::apply_rotary_emb()` 的 complex multiply 等价于：

```text
正向:
even' = even * cos - odd * sin
odd'  = even * sin + odd * cos

inverse:
even' = even * cos + odd * sin
odd'  = odd * cos - even * sin
```

当前 V4 路径中：

- `qkv_proj_rope.py` 的 Q/KV RoPE 与正向公式一致。
- decode/prefill compressor 的 KV rope 与正向公式一致，只要调用方提供的 cos/sin position 正确。
- `decode_sparse_attn.py` 和 `prefill_sparse_attn.py` 的 output rope slice 与 inverse 公式一致。
- 主要需要额外确认的是 decode indexer/inner indexer compressor 的 per-batch half table 设计，在 `S > 1` 或 compressed position 不等于 first token position 时是否和 `model.py` 完全等价。

## 实现方案

新增 host-side helper module：

```text
models/deepseek/v4/rope_tables.py
```

该模块不定义 `pl.jit` kernel。它只负责 host/runtime 侧 table 生成与 materialization。

建议 API：

```python
def rope_profile_for_compress_ratio(config, compress_ratio):
    """Return (base, original_seq_len) for this layer profile."""


def build_deepseek_v4_rope_tables(
    config,
    compress_ratio,
    *,
    max_seq_len=None,
    rope_dim=None,
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    device=None,
):
    """Return (freqs_cos, freqs_sin), both shaped [max_seq_len, rope_dim]."""


def build_layer_rope_tables(config, layer_id, *, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=None):
    """Select compress_ratio from config.compress_ratios[layer_id]."""


def materialize_token_rope_tables(freqs_cos, freqs_sin, position_ids):
    """Return token-local (cos, sin) tables shaped [T, rope_dim]."""
```

### Profile 选择

与 `model.py` 保持一致：

```text
compress_ratio == 0:
  base = config.rope_theta
  original_seq_len = 0
  # 禁用 YaRN

compress_ratio != 0:
  base = config.compress_rope_theta
  original_seq_len = config.original_max_position_embeddings
  # 当 original_seq_len > 0 时启用 YaRN 修正
```

因此 full-model runtime 至少应缓存两类表：

- SWA table：`compress_ratio = 0`
- compressed-layer table：`compress_ratio = 4` / `128`，二者 RoPE profile 相同，只要 config 和 max_seq_len/rope_dim 相同即可复用

推荐 cache key：

```text
(config.name, max_seq_len, rope_dim, compress_ratio == 0 ? "swa" : "compressed", dtype, device)
```

### 频率生成算法

保留 `model.py` 的 YaRN inverse-frequency 修正逻辑，但输出 real cos/sin，不生成 complex tensor。

```text
inv_freq[i] = 1 / base ** (2 * i / dim)
i in [0, dim / 2)
```

当 `original_seq_len > 0`：

```text
correction_dim(rot) =
    dim * log(original_seq_len / (rot * 2*pi)) / (2 * log(base))

low  = floor(correction_dim(beta_fast))
high = ceil(correction_dim(beta_slow))
low/high clamp 到 [0, dim - 1]

ramp[i] = clamp((i - low) / (high - low), 0, 1)
smooth[i] = 1 - ramp[i]

inv_freq[i] =
    inv_freq[i] / factor * (1 - smooth[i]) + inv_freq[i] * smooth[i]
```

然后：

```text
angle[pos, i] = pos * inv_freq[i]
cos_half = cos(angle)
sin_half = sin(angle)
```

最终返回：

```text
freqs_cos = concat(cos_half, cos_half)  # [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM]
freqs_sin = concat(sin_half, sin_half)  # [MAX_SEQ_LEN, ROPE_HEAD_DIM]
```

注意：

- inverse frequencies、angles、cos/sin 计算使用 FP32。
- 只在 cos/sin 完成后 cast 到 BF16。
- 不在 V4 path 中返回 complex `freqs_cis`。
- 不新增 PyPTO device kernel 来生成整张 RoPE table；table 是只依赖 config 的常量，适合 host/runtime 侧预计算后作为普通 device input 传给 kernel。

### 调用点迁移

1. 替换 `models/deepseek/v4` 中 fixture 的 synthetic `cos(arange * 1e-3)` / `sin(arange * 1e-3)` 初始化。

2. 对接收 full table 的模块，直接使用：

```python
freqs_cos, freqs_sin = build_deepseek_v4_rope_tables(config, compress_ratio)
```

3. 对 token-local 接口，使用：

```python
full_cos, full_sin = build_deepseek_v4_rope_tables(config, compress_ratio)
token_cos, token_sin = materialize_token_rope_tables(full_cos, full_sin, position_ids)
```

4. 对 decode compressor/indexer standalone test 的 `[B, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2]` 输入，应从 full table 中按对应 absolute position 取：

```python
cos = full_cos.index_select(0, batch_positions)[:, :ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2].float()
sin = full_sin.index_select(0, batch_positions)[:, :ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2].float()
```

其中 `batch_positions` 需要根据模块语义分别是：

- decode compressor：compressed write position
- decode indexer query：query token position
- decode inner indexer compressor：inner compressed write position

## 测试用例设计

### 1. Table 生成与 `model.py::precompute_freqs_cis()` 对齐

新增 focused unit test，分别覆盖：

- `compress_ratio = 0`
  - `base = rope_theta`
  - `original_seq_len = 0`
  - YaRN disabled
- `compress_ratio = 4`
  - `base = compress_rope_theta`
  - `original_seq_len = original_max_position_embeddings`
  - YaRN enabled when original length > 0
- `compress_ratio = 128`
  - 与 compressed profile 一致

断言：

```python
freqs_cis = model.precompute_freqs_cis(
    dim=rope_dim,
    seqlen=max_seq_len,
    original_seq_len=expected_original_seq_len,
    base=expected_base,
    factor=config.rope_factor,
    beta_fast=config.beta_fast,
    beta_slow=config.beta_slow,
)

freqs_cos, freqs_sin = build_deepseek_v4_rope_tables(...)

assert_allclose(freqs_cos[:, :rope_dim // 2].float(), freqs_cis.real.float())
assert_allclose(freqs_sin[:, :rope_dim // 2].float(), freqs_cis.imag.float())
assert_allclose(freqs_cos[:, rope_dim // 2:].float(), freqs_cos[:, :rope_dim // 2].float())
assert_allclose(freqs_sin[:, rope_dim // 2:].float(), freqs_sin[:, :rope_dim // 2].float())
```

### 2. 正向 RoPE apply 与 `model.py::apply_rotary_emb()` 对齐

构造随机 BF16 tensor：

- Q path shape example: `[B, S, H, ROPE_HEAD_DIM]`
- KV path shape example: `[B, S, ROPE_HEAD_DIM]`

用 `model.py::apply_rotary_emb(x, freqs_cis)` 得到 reference。

再用 real cos/sin 展开公式得到 V4 语义结果：

```python
x_pair = x.float().unflatten(-1, (-1, 2))
even = x_pair[..., 0]
odd = x_pair[..., 1]
cos = freqs_cos[pos, :half]
sin = freqs_sin[pos, :half]

out_even = even * cos - odd * sin
out_odd = even * sin + odd * cos
out = stack(out_even, out_odd).flatten(-2)
```

断言与 complex reference 一致。

### 3. Inverse RoPE apply 与 `inverse=True` 对齐

同样构造随机 attention output rope slice，比较：

```python
model.apply_rotary_emb(x_ref, freqs_cis, inverse=True)
```

和 real cos/sin inverse 展开公式：

```text
even' = even * cos + odd * sin
odd'  = odd * cos - even * sin
```

用于覆盖 `decode_sparse_attn.py` / `prefill_sparse_attn.py` 的 de-rotation 语义。

### 4. Position materialization 测试

覆盖：

- full table -> token-local `[T, ROPE_HEAD_DIM]`
- full table -> per-batch half `[B, ROPE_HEAD_DIM // 2]`
- compressed write position：

```text
cmp_pos = write_pos + 1 - COMPRESS_RATIO
```

断言 materialized rows 与 full table 对应行一致。

### 5. Regression tests for existing kernels

替换 fixture 初始化后，至少跑以下路径各一个 standalone kernel：

- SWA：`decode_attention_swa.py` 或 `prefill_attention_swa.py`
- CSA：`decode_attention_csa.py` 或 `prefill_attention_csa.py`
- HCA：`decode_attention_hca.py` 或 `prefill_attention_hca.py`
- token-local sparse：`decode_sparse_attn.py` 或 `prefill_sparse_attn.py`
- standalone qkv：`qkv_proj_rope.py`
- compressor/indexer fixture：
  - `prefill_compressor_ratio4.py`
  - `prefill_compressor_ratio128.py`
  - `prefill_indexer_compressor.py`
  - decode compressor/indexer standalone tests after confirming correct position selection

## 验收标准

- V4 path 有统一的 host-side RoPE/YaRN table builder。
- 不再依赖 synthetic `cos(arange * 1e-3)` 来模拟 DeepSeek RoPE。
- 生成的 `freqs_cos/freqs_sin` 与 `model.py::precompute_freqs_cis()` 的 real/imag 部分一致。
- V4 正向 RoPE 和 inverse RoPE 展开公式与 `model.py::apply_rotary_emb()` / `inverse=True` 对齐。
- SWA 和 compressed layers 使用正确且不同的 RoPE profiles。
- kernel signatures 尽量保持不变。
- 不新增用于整表生成的 PyPTO device kernel。

title: perf(dsv4 decode_sparse_attn): stage compressed gather_kv in UB for coalesced stores
body:
## What

`gather_kv` is the heaviest kernel in decode sparse attention and is MTE-bound — a pure `GM->UB->GM` copy with Vec/Scalar idle. The per-row `GM->GM` copy serializes `MTE2`(load) and `MTE3`(store): codegen caps the `GM->GM` ping-pong at 2-deep buffering regardless of `pl.pipeline` stage, so the two engines run **fully serial** (`MTE2_busy + MTE3_busy ≈ wall`).

This stages each `GATHER_FILL_TILE` block of the compressed region in a UB tile, then flushes it with one wide store:
- every scattered load gets its own tile row → no buffer-reuse WAR → loads **stream on MTE2** instead of ping-ponging with MTE3 per row;
- the many 1-row stores **coalesce into one block store**;
- the tile is Vec-zeroed (Vec was idle), and `-1` / padding-tail slots keep that zero.

## Result

Kernel-insight (msprof op-sim, one token-block, `compress_ratio=4`):

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| gather_kv wall | 231.6 | **170.5 (−26%)** |
| MTE2 util | 59% | 81% |
| MTE3 busy | 92.6 | 25.1 |

`MTE2` (scattered 1-row loads, not coalescable) is the new floor at 137.9, so the kernel is now close to load-bound.

## Notes

- The **window** block still reads `ori_kv_flat` (a reshape of the self-touched INOUT `ori_kv`) and could not be staged the same way without a miscompile, so it stays per-row. Minimal probes of the staging idiom (conditional, if/else two-source, 128-row tiles, INOUT+self-touch) all pass in isolation, so the cause looks specific to that tensor's interaction — left as a follow-up.
- `tools/export_all_kernel_insight.py`: also resolve C-linkage device kernels (which demangle to a bare name) when a host `Launch*` wrapper coexists, so per-func insight export works on current builds.

## Test

Validated against golden on `a2a3sim` across `compress_ratio {0,4,128}` and the `short-window` / `mixed-topk` / `overlay-replacement` / `causal-regression` fixtures — all pass.

title: perf(dsv4 prefill): coarsen compressor state_update (CSA -41.6%, HCA -9.8%) + re-apply hc_post/rope opts
body:
## What & why

DeepSeek-V4 prefill attention perf on the unified base: two measured speedups
plus profiling flags and guards. Numbers are remote NPU (a2a3),
`--enable-l2-swimlane` **without** `--enable-dep-gen` (dep_gen capture overhead
scales with task count and would overstate the gain), 3 iterations, golden PASS,
non-overlapping before/after distributions.

### 1. Coarsen compressor `state_update` writeback to per-token (main win)

`prefill_c4_state_update` / `prefill_hca_c128_state_update` were `pl.spmd` over
`MAX_TOKENS * out_blocks` (4096 / 2048 tiny per-(token, out-block) tasks) -- a
dispatch-bound state-cache writeback that sits on the kernel-completion tail
even though its output (`cmp_kv_state`/`score_state`) is not consumed by the
attention. Coarsened to `pl.spmd(MAX_TOKENS)`; c128 writes the whole
`MAIN_OUT_DIM` state row in one vector op, c4 loops the out-blocks inside one
task. Math and the zero-weighted pool-ordering dep are unchanged.

- CSA `prefill_c4_state_update`: **4096 -> 128 events, span 1761 -> 69 us** (swimlane).
- **CSA Total Test Time median 3226.6 -> 1882.9 us (-41.6%)**
- **HCA Total Test Time median 1801.2 -> 1624.1 us (-9.8%)**

### 2. Vectorize hc_post post/comb mix

2-D block ops (`D_CHUNK` 512 -> 256, `row_expand_mul` over `[TILE, 1]` columns).
**SWA Total Test Time median 1633.9 -> 1558.5 us (-4.6%)**.

### 3. Profiling flags + guards (no perf impact)

- `--enable-dep-gen` on `prefill_attention_{swa,hca,csa}`, `--enable-pmu` on
  `prefill_moe`. The unified dynamic-shape kernels record AICore L2-swimlane
  tasks with `func_id == -1`, so a `deps.json` (dep_gen) is required to recover
  function names in the swimlane / dependency view.
- `assert HC_MULT == 4` in `hc_pre` / `hc_post` (both mixes are hand-unrolled
  for HC_MULT == 4; the local UB tiles need literal compile-time-constant
  subscripts, so this cannot be parameterized with `pl.unroll`). `assert
  D % D_CHUNK == 0` in `hc_post`. No-op today (all configs use `hc_mult == 4`,
  `D % D_CHUNK == 0`).

## Correctness

- `hc_post` / SWA / HCA / CSA: end-to-end `x_out` golden PASS on a2a3.
- The compressor `state_update` output is **not** consumed by the attention, so
  the end-to-end `x_out` golden does not cover it. Verified separately via the
  standalone `prefill_compressor_ratio4` / `prefill_compressor_ratio128` tests
  (`kv_state` / `score_state` / `cmp_kv` golden PASS at `max_error_ratio=0.0`).

## CI note

The `sim (a2a3sim)` / `sim (a5sim)` jobs fail with `RuntimeError: g++-15 not
found` -- a missing compiler on the sim runners (hits every kernel that builds,
incl. `prefill_moe.py` which this PR only adds a CLI flag to). The real `a2a3`
hardware job passes. Not caused by this PR.

## Summary

This PR adds monolithic DeepSeek V4 prefill single-layer EP2 graphs for SWA, HCA, and CSA.

The new graph entrypoints wire the existing packed prefill attention modules into the MoE EP path:

```text
hc_pre -> attn_norm -> qkv/rope -> attention/compressor/indexer -> cache writeback -> hc_post -> active-token select -> moe_ep
```

The implementation keeps the current token-major packed prefill contract and removes the need for split/attention-only/MoE-only drivers in this bring-up path.

title: fix(dsv4 decode_sparse_attn): revert proj_b to no-split (drop accidental LEFT_RIGHT)
body:
## What

#539 unintentionally bundled an unrelated change: it switched the `proj_b` output-projection scope from the default no-split to `pl.split(pl.SplitMode.LEFT_RIGHT)`:

```python
-    for nb in pl.spmd(D // B_N_TILE, name_hint="proj_b"):
+    for nb in pl.spmd(D // B_N_TILE, name_hint="proj_b",
+                      optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.LEFT_RIGHT)]):
```

That change originated in a fork-local "balance proj_b dequant across both AIV cores" commit that was never in upstream; it rode into #539 via the PR's rebase base, so the merged PR carried it in addition to the intended gather_kv change.

## Why it's a bug

The `LEFT_RIGHT` column-half of the mixed cube+vec INT8 GEMM + per-channel dequant epilogue miscomputes on the dual-AIV hardware path, producing **precision errors in the decode `swa` / `hca` / `csa` attention outputs**. It is shared by all three (it's the output projection), which is why even `swa` — whose `gather_kv` is byte-identical to fa1f5b1 (`TOPK == WIN`, the staging path is not emitted) — regressed.

`a2a3sim` collapses `LEFT_RIGHT` to a correct single-lane path, so it passed in sim / standalone golden — the error only shows on device.

## Fix

Revert `proj_b` to the no-split form used in `fa1f5b1`, **keeping #539's `gather_kv` UB-staging change intact**. Net effect versus `fa1f5b1` is now the gather change only — exactly what #539 intended.

## Note

The dual-AIV `proj_b` balancing is a real optimization, but it needs `pypto`'s `LEFT_RIGHT` split to handle this mixed cube+vec + per-channel-scale epilogue correctly first; that is a separate `pypto`-side fix and can be reintroduced afterwards.

title: [Feature] TurboQuant — PolarQuant INT4 KV Cache for Qwen3-14B
body:
### Summary

# TurboQuant — PolarQuant INT4 KV Cache for Qwen3-14B

## File Layout

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `turboquant_kv.py` | Lloyd-Max codebook solver + quantize function + dequant function |
| `qwen3_14b_prefill_tq.py` | Prefill end-to-end: quantize K/V → write cache → dequant for attention |
| `qwen3_14b_decode_tq.py` | Decode end-to-end: read quantized cache → dequant → attention |Duplicate of #

## End-to-End Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Prefill (compress)                           │
│                                                                  │
│  K/V proj ──► RoPE(K) / L2 norm ──► rotate ──► INT4 quantize    │
│                                         │                        │
│                write quant_k/v_cache ◄───┘                       │
│                                         │                        │
│             Attention reads ──► dequant ◄┘                       │
│                                                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                     Decode (decompress)                          │
│                                                                  │
│   read INT4 from quant_k/v_cache ──► dequant ──► Attention      │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Quantization

### 1. Lloyd-Max Codebook (computed once at module load)

`solve_lloyd_max(head_dim, bits=4)` in `turboquant_kv.py` solves for the
optimal 16-level scalar quantizer under `N(0, 1/head_dim)`:

- **Input**: distribution std `σ = 1/sqrt(head_dim)`
- **Algorithm**: Lloyd-Max iteration (alternating boundary and centroid updates)
  - Step 1: boundaries = midpoints of adjacent centroids
  - Step 2: centroids = Gaussian conditional mean `E[X | a < X < b]`
    (computed analytically via `torch.erf`)
- **Output**: `_lm_centroids` [16] centroids, `_lm_boundaries` [15] decision boundaries
- The 15 boundary values are unpacked into `_b0`…`_b14` for use in kernel comparisons

### 2. Quantize Kernel (`turboquant_kv_prefill` — `@pl.jit.inline`)

Executes 4 scopes per KV head during prefill:

```
Scope A: K RoPE + L2 norm + normalize
  ├─ K RoPE (cos/sin rotary transform)
  ├─ L2 norm = sqrt(sum(x²) + ε) per row
  ├─ normalize: x / L2_norm → BF16, write to k_norm_buf
  └─ L2 norm written to k_scales_buf

Scope B: K rotate + Lloyd-Max quantize
  ├─ k_norm_buf × rot_matrix → k_rot (BF16×BF16→FP32)
  ├─ 15-way boundary search: cumulative GE (≥_b0) + … + (≥_b14)
  │   → INT4 index in [0, 15]
  └─ FP32→INT32→FP16→UINT8, write to quant_k_temp

Scope C: V L2 norm + normalize (no RoPE for V)
  ├─ L2 norm = sqrt(sum(x²) + ε)
  ├─ normalize → BF16, write to v_norm_buf
  └─ L2 norm written to v_scales_buf

Scope D: V rotate + Lloyd-Max quantize
  └─ same as Scope B, write to quant_v_temp
```

Quantized outputs:

| Output | Shape | Dtype | Description |
|--------|-------|-------|-------------|
| `quant_k/v_cache` | [total_rows, HEAD_DIM] | UINT8 | INT4 indices, range [0, 15] |
| `quant_k/v_scales` | [total_rows, 1] | FP32 | per-row L2 norm |

## Dequantization

### `turboquant_kv_dequant_chunk` — `@pl.jit.inline`

Dequantizes one CMP_CHUNK (32 rows) of INT4 KV cache. All three steps are
inlined into the caller's `pl.at` scope:

```
Step 1: Gather (codebook lookup)
  UINT8 indices → FP16 cast → INT32 cast → pl.gather(codebook) → FP32 centroids

Step 2: Renormalize + Scale
  centroid → rsqrt(row_sum(sq) + ε) normalize to unit sphere → × stored L2 scale

Step 3: Unrotate (rotate back to original space)
  → BF16 cast → matmul(rot_slice^T) → BF16 → write to out_bf16
```

### Prefill QK attention (dequant K on the fly)

```python
with pl.at("qk_dequant"):
    for each CMP_CHUNK (4 iterations for BLOCK_SIZE=128):
        chunk_out = pl.create_tensor([32, 128], BF16)
        turboquant_kv_dequant_chunk(indices, scales, codebook, rot, chunk_out)
        k_bf16_buf = pl.assemble(chunk_out)  # directly BF16, no extra cast

with pl.at("qk_matmul"):
    raw_scores = pl.matmul(q_padded, k_bf16_buf, b_trans=True)
```

### Prefill SV attention (dequant V on the fly)

```python
with pl.at("sv_dequant"):
    for each CMP_CHUNK:
        chunk_out = pl.create_tensor([32, 128], BF16)
        turboquant_kv_dequant_chunk(indices, scales, codebook, rot, chunk_out)
        v_tile_full = pl.assemble(chunk_out)  # directly BF16

with pl.at("sv_matmul"):
    oi_tmp = pl.matmul(exp_tile, v_tile_full)
```

### Decode dequant

Identical to prefill, using `BLOCK_SIZE=128` (same as `SEQ_TILE`).

## Key Constants

| Constant | Value | Notes |
|----------|-------|-------|
| `N_LEVELS` | 16 | INT4, 16 quantization levels |
| `CMP_CHUNK` | 32 | Dequant sub-chunk rows (32×1B = 32-byte aligned) |
| `SEQ_TILE` / `BLOCK_SIZE` | 128 | Attention sequence tile |
| `TOK_TILE` | 16 | Prefill quantize token tile |
| `CMP_TILE` / `CMP_TILE_SV` | 64 | Dequant sub-tile |
| `HEAD_DIM` | 128 | Q/K/V head dimension (rotation → Gaussian for d≥64) |

## Dependency Graph

```
turboquant_kv.py  ──►  qwen3_14b_prefill_tq.py  (prefill_layer_tq)
                   ──►  qwen3_14b_decode_tq.py   (decode_layer_tq)

Exported symbols:
  - solve_lloyd_max(d, bits)           # CPU-side Lloyd-Max solver
  - _lm_centroids, _lm_boundaries      # Module-level codebook
  - turboquant_kv_prefill(...)         # Quantize (prefill only)
  - turboquant_kv_dequant_chunk(...)   # Dequant (shared by prefill & decode)
```

## Design Decisions

1. **Shared rotation matrix across prefill and decode**: `rot_matrices` is
   generated once via `torch.linalg.qr(torch.randn(head_dim, head_dim))`
   (seed=42) and shared between quantization and dequantization to ensure
   the rotated domain is consistent.

2. **BF16 dequant output**: avoids extra `pl.cast` at call sites, saving
   one buffer and one scope per attention operation.

3. **No internal `pl.at` in inline dequant function**:
   `turboquant_kv_dequant_chunk` does not contain `pl.at` scopes. All
   ops are inlined into the caller's scope, avoiding nested InCore
   functions that the compiler cannot resolve (call directions between
   nested scopes are undefined).

4. **Renormalize corrects quantization drift**: centroid vectors gathered
   from the codebook are not guaranteed to lie on the unit sphere.
   Dequant always renormalizes via `rsqrt(row_sum(sq) + EPS)` before
   rescaling, preserving numerical stability.


### Motivation / Use Case

TurboQuant compresses the KV cache to INT4, reducing memory usage to 1/4 of
BF16. It is based on **PolarQuant**: scalar quantization via Lloyd-Max in a
randomly-rotated space. After rotation by a random orthogonal matrix, each
coordinate of a `d`-dimensional unit vector follows approximately
`N(0, 1/head_dim)` (for `d >= 64`), enabling near-optimal quantization.

### Proposed API / Behavior

_No response_

title: perf(dsv4): hc_pre sinkhorn group-stack + mix_x sequential accumulate (-5.6%)
body:
## What

Two composable optimizations to the fused single-spmd `hc_pre` vector epilogue (`models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py`):

1. **comb sinkhorn — group-stack.** Stack the 4 comb groups col-wise (`pl.concat`) into a padded `[T_TILE, hc*8]` tile and `reshape` to `[T_TILE*hc, 8]` so each group becomes one row. The 20-iteration Sinkhorn loop's per-group `4x row_sum` / `4x row_expand_div` then collapse to a **single op each** (the loop is latency-bound on tiny `[16,4]` tiles). Padded columns stay zero throughout → **bit-identical** to the per-group form.
2. **mix_x — sequential head accumulate.** Accumulate the 4 heads sequentially (`load → cast → weighted-add → free`) instead of materializing all 4 `x_fp32` + 4 `y` tiles at once. This cuts the Vec live-set ~3x, freeing enough UB to raise `D_TILE 256 → 512` (one 512B L2 line), which drops the AIV critical-path task from **~107 → ~96us**. The left-to-right sum order also matches the torch reference's `y += x[:,h]*pre[:,h]`.

Net **−18 lines** (the stacked sinkhorn is shorter than the 4-group unroll).

## Why

Swimlane analysis showed `hc_pre` is **AIV-bound** (not matmul-bound): the heavy AIV subblock (~107us, mix_x + sinkhorn) dominates while the cube matmul is only ~58us. These two changes attack both the sinkhorn op-count and the mix_x HBM/UB pressure.

## Validation (a2a3 real device, decode B=64 S=2 and prefill B=1 S=128, both T=128)

- **Precision:** `x_mixed` / `comb` / `post` all PASS, decode + prefill, repeatedly.
- **Perf (same-session interleaved A/B, 4 rounds, every new run beats its paired baseline):**
  - End-to-end (AICore, incl. AICPU dispatch): **166.4 → 157.2us (−5.6%)**
  - AICore compute span: **127 → 116us (−8.6%)**; AIV max task **113 → 100us (−12%)**

The end-to-end gain is smaller than the compute gain because ~41.5us of the standalone test's wall is fixed AICPU dispatch overhead (24 core-task dispatches), which this change does not touch; in the full CSA orchestrator that overhead is amortized across the pipeline.

title: Update: Qwen3-14B decode FP32 inter-layer carry + fused layer output
body:
## Summary
- Carry the inter-layer hidden as FP32 (was BF16), dropping per-layer BF16 rounding for more precise decode numerics (golden argmax is the sanity check, not bit-equality).
- Fuse the layer output and the next layer's x*gamma into one `dcr_xgamma` task (DOWN_ON-way): emit `out` (residual) and `normed_out` (x*gamma) from the same in-register chunk, removing the `out_partial` scratch + extra copy task and the GM round-trip for x_gamma.
- Whole-layer manual scope (x_gamma..rope) with explicit `deps=` edges; cross-iteration TaskId carries (`prev_out_tids` / `prev_normed_tids`) gate the next layer's seeds / QKV. `copy_hidden` casts the external BF16 embed input -> FP32 to seed layer 0; `cast_lmhead_in` casts the final FP32 hidden -> BF16 for the unchanged `rms_lm_head`.
- `QKV_OK` 4 -> 5 (`QKV_K_SLICE=1024`, 1:1 partial-Q split).
- KV cache stays PAGED (`block_table` read / `slot_mapping` write, `SEQ_TILE` == serving page_size 128): the per-layer cache base and block-table row stride are derived from the runtime-dynamic pool dims, so decode reads the same paged pool prefill writes. (An intermediate contiguous-pool detour was reverted within this branch.)
- `--enable-l2-swimlane` becomes an optional integer `PERF_LEVEL` (was a bare boolean flag): bare flag selects level 4 (full); levels 1=AICore timing, 2=+dispatch/fanout, 3=+sched phases, 4=+orch phases; 0 (default) disables. Lets swimlane capture granularity be tuned per run.

title: perf(dsv4 decode_sparse_attn): UP_DOWN-split proj_b to balance AIV epilogue (-16%)
body:
## What

Add `optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)]` to the `proj_b` spmd region in
`models/deepseek/v4/decode_sparse_attn.py` (INT8 output projection + per-channel dequant).

## Why — proj_b was AIV-unbalanced

`proj_b` is a mixed cube+vector region: an INT8 GEMM (`o_r_i8 @ wo_b^T`) followed by a
per-row × per-channel dequant epilogue. Without a split, each spmd task's dequant epilogue
was distributed unevenly across the core group's **two AIV cores** — one vector lane became a
straggler and the whole `proj_b` region waited on it. The cube GEMM is small (INT8) and
finished early, so the region wall was set almost entirely by that unbalanced AIV epilogue.

`pl.split` halves each task so the cube works one half while the two AIVs run the epilogue on
the other half, balanced one-half-per-AIV and overlapped with the cube.

## Result (a2a3, 12 interleaved rounds, paired per round)

`proj_b` **region wall** read from the L2 swimlane; every run validates against golden.

| proj_b | region wall | vs no-split | AIV duration CV |
|---|---|---|---|
| no-split (current) | 238 µs | baseline | 0.74 (unbalanced) |
| **UP_DOWN (this PR)** | **200 µs** | **−16 %** (faster in 12/12 rounds) | 0.47 |
| LEFT_RIGHT | 309 µs | +30 % (slower in 12/12 rounds) | 0.55 |

Both split axes balance the two AIVs (CV drops), but only **UP_DOWN** turns that into a region
speedup.

## Why UP_DOWN, not LEFT_RIGHT

The BF16 output store `attn_out[b_tb:+B_T_TILE, n0:+B_N_TILE]` is already only **256 B** on its
innermost axis (`B_N_TILE = 128`, below the 512 B L2 line).

- **LEFT_RIGHT** halves the *columns* → **128 B** store. The narrower store straddles cache
  lines even more, ~doubling MTE3-bound AIV time and making the region **+30 % slower** despite
  the better balance. (This is the "accidental LEFT_RIGHT" that #543 reverted to no-split —
  confirmed here to be a regression, not just a correctness risk.)
- **UP_DOWN** halves the *rows* → store keeps its **256 B** width, so it balances the two AIVs
  without touching store granularity. Net **−16 %**.

The `report/perf_hints.log` line for the store confirms it at compile time: 256 B for
no-split/UP_DOWN vs 128 B for LEFT_RIGHT.

Note: the usual UB-overflow rationale for splitting does **not** apply here — no-split
`proj_b_aiv` already fits at 87.9 % of the 192 KB Vec budget (no spill). The win is purely
AIV balancing + cube/vec overlap.

## Sibling kernels

`decode_sparse_attn_swa.py` and `decode_sparse_attn_hca.py` carry a byte-identical no-split
`proj_b`, so the same UP_DOWN split should give them the same ~−16 %. Left out of this PR for
separate validation, but worth applying.

title: perf(dsv4 decode_sparse_attn gather_kv): coalesce dead-store + rebalance compressed staging
body:
## What

Two `gather_kv` optimizations for the DSV4 unified decode sparse-attention layer (CSA), plus a kernel-insight export tooling fix.

### gather_kv: coalesce dead-store + rebalance compressed staging (commit 1)

`gather_kv` is ~48% of the decode wall. Two changes, **combined -1.78%** of the decode wall on a2a3 (72645 -> 71355 sim-cycles, from the L2 swimlane):

- **Dead-store coalesce**: bulk-zero only the window block `[0, WIN)`. The compressed blocks `[WIN, PADDED_TOPK)` are fully rewritten by the zero-initialized staging block stores, so zeroing them up front was a dead store (~4 of 5 stores/token). The SWA path (no compressed staging) still zeroes the whole region. **-1.07% alone.**
- **Wave rebalance**: run the compressed staging as a separate, finer SPMD over `(token, fill-block)` units (`T*N_CMP_BLK = 512` vs the per-token `128`) so the gather fills the 48 AIV cores more evenly across waves (tail-wave imbalance ~1.5x -> ~1.1x). **+0.71% on top.** `qk_pv` correctly waits for both the window pass and the compressed pass.

### export_all_kernel_insight tooling (commit 2)

- Run each msprof child in its own session and tear the whole process group down on the script's own timeout, so the long-running simulator grandchild can't reparent to init and keep burning a CPU core after a failure.
- Default the task-submit invocation to `--max-time 0` (new `--task-max-time`, default 0) so the queue's 300s cap doesn't truncate long case runs / msprof sweeps.

## Validation

Golden-validated on a2a3 (`ratio_allclose`):

- **CSA** (`decode_sparse_attn.py`): PASS — default + short-window (SWA path) + mixed-topk + overlay-replacement + causal-regression fixtures.
- **SWA** (`decode_sparse_attn_swa.py`): PASS (file unchanged; regression check).
- **HCA** (`decode_sparse_attn_hca.py`): PASS (file unchanged; regression check).

title: Revert #545: hc_pre sinkstack/mix_x breaks decode_attention_swa x_out
body:
## Why

PR #545 (`9ec1a5c`, hc_pre sinkhorn group-stack + mix_x sequential accumulate, -5.6%) introduced a **deterministic precision regression** in `models/deepseek/v4/decode_attention_swa.py`.

### Repro / evidence
`python models/deepseek/v4/decode_attention_swa.py -p a2a3`

- `x_out` **FAIL** `ratio_reldiff`: error_count ≈ 8–10% of elements (threshold 0.5%), **6/6 runs** — not intermittent.
- `kv_cache` still **PASS** every run → regression is on the hc_pre → attention output path, not KV writeback.
- Error shape is small & dense (abs_diff ≈ 0.01–0.016, rdiff ≈ 1–13% on ~10% of elements) → an accumulation/precision-order change, not a race.
- Reproduced both before and **after** a fresh underlying `pypto` update → not a compiler-version artifact.

### Bisect
Only `hc_pre.py` changed between `a238081` (good) and the broken tip; the sole commit touching it is `9ec1a5c` (#545). Reverting `hc_pre.py` to its pre-#545 form restores `x_out` **PASS 3/3** (and 6/6 incl. updated pypto).

## What this does
Reverts `9ec1a5c` (touches only `hc_pre.py`). The reverted file is byte-identical to the known-good `a238081` version that passes 6/6.

## Trade-off
Gives back #545's -5.6% perf in exchange for correctness, until hc_pre sinkstack/mix_x can be re-implemented precision-safe (likely the `mix_x` sequential-accumulate path).

title: CI: scope PR tests by reverse-import closure

title: refactor(dsv4 moe): quant-faithful FP4/FP8 expert weight fixtures
body:
## Summary
- Replace the `randn`+lognormal `gen_int8_weight` with generators that simulate the real DeepSeek-V4-Flash quant grids, so synthetic expert fixtures match the measured INT8 weight distribution instead of a benign Gaussian.
- `gen_routed_weight` (expert_routed.py): MXFP4 grid (e2m1, per-32-group E8M0 scale) → ~37 discrete levels, ~11.6% zero spike, scale CV ~0.09.
- `gen_shared_weight` (expert_shared.py): MXFP8 grid (e4m3, 128×128-block E8M0 scale) + per-output-channel gain → ~200 levels, scale CV ~0.5/0.35.
- Each module owns its generator (no cross-import); `moe.py` / `moe_ep.py` import both inside `build_tensor_specs`.
- Standalone expert tests use the real dequant magnitude; `moe` / `moe_ep` keep the smaller behaviorally-calibrated magnitude, since their `x_next` integration metric is dominated by near-zero residual cancellations that random fixtures cannot reproduce at the real magnitude.
- Verified on a2a3: `expert_routed`, `expert_shared`, `moe` (layer 7) PASS; `moe_ep` compile-only PASS.

title: fix(dsv4 qkv): drop qr pre-quant bf16 round to match cann mla_prolog
body:
## Summary
- Drop the `qr` pre-quant BF16 round in `qkv_proj_rope`: the q-LoRA RMSNorm output was rounded FP32 -> BF16 -> FP32 before the per-token INT8 quant, in both the kernel (amax + quant passes) and the golden. cann's `mla_prolog_quant` keeps `qr` in FP32 through the INT8 quant.
- This BF16 round was the dominant source of the W8A8 q-proj error on realistic weight distributions: the kernel-vs-golden `q` metric exceeded the 0.5% standalone gate under real DeepSeek-V4-Flash weights (~1.2-1.6%) and under cann's uniform init (~1.1%). Quantizing `qr` from FP32 directly drops it to ~0% (q rel-L2 falls ~20-57x); `kv`/`qr`/`qr_scale` unchanged.
- Align the `qkv_proj_rope` fixtures with cann's `test_mla_prolog_quant_pypto` `gen_mla_prolog_input_data` (uniform init for x / wq_a / wq_b / wkv / gamma / cos / sin), replacing the randn + ones-gamma + real-RoPE-table init, so the standalone test exercises the same input regime as cann.
- Verified on a2a3: `q`/`kv`/`qr`/`qr_scale` PASS with the new init; real-weight and cann-uniform `q` both pass the 0.5% gate.

title: perf(qwen3-14b): dcr_xgamma as one pl.spmd dispatch (fix WAW serial)
body:
## Summary
- `dcr_xgamma` was `DOWN_ON` separate `pl.parallel` `pl.at` tasks, each writing a disjoint slice of `out` / `normed_out`. The intended 5-way parallelism (per the in-code comment, via `OptimizeOrchTensors` Pattern-5 out-window externalization) did NOT fire on device — the writers WAW-serialized on the shared tensors and ran on ONE core (~25us at the chunk tail, ~45us span at every layer boundary, measured in the L2 swimlane).
- Root cause: `OutWindowExternalizer` bails (`HasUnwindowableSiblingOutputWriter` / `HasDuplicateExternalizedOutputParent`) when a parallel task writes multiple outputs. The dcr + next-layer-x_gamma fusion writes TWO outputs (`out` + `normed_out`), so the externalization is skipped, the writes stay full-tensor, and the runtime tensormap serializes them WAW.
- Fix: convert `dcr_xgamma` to a single `pl.spmd(DOWN_ON)` dispatch, whose grid blocks are parallel by construction (like `x_gamma`'s disjoint `normed_states` writes) — no static disjointness proof needed. The disjoint-slice writes now run on `DOWN_ON` cores (~4us). The fusion is kept (still one task writing `out` + `normed_out`, no extra GM round-trip). The dispatch deps on all `down_proj` tids and carries one dispatch tid for both outputs across all `DOWN_ON` slabs into `prev_out_tids` / `prev_normed_tids`.

Measured (2-layer decode, no lm_head): makespan 2114.6us → 2090.4us; the 5 dcr writers go from serial-on-one-core to parallel-on-5-cores at every layer boundary and at the chunk tail.

Correctness unchanged: single-layer golden PASS (seed 1234); 2-layer fused `decode_fwd` argmax 16/16, logits 100% within 5e-2. The dcr math is identical — only the dispatch shape changed.

None

title: [Feature] dsv4 prefill: single-request CSA/HCA/SWA attention + batch/seq splitting in prefill_layer
body:
### Summary

Make the three DeepSeek-V4 prefill attention kernels (`prefill_attention_csa` /
`prefill_attention_hca` / `prefill_attention_swa`) **single-request**: each
invocation handles one contiguous run of `T <= 128` tokens belonging to one
request (`num_reqs = 1`). Move the per-request loop and long-prompt chunking up
into `prefill_layer`, which owns the #382 packed metadata contract
(`cu_q_lens` / `token_to_request` / `position_ids`) and feeds each attention
call a single-request slice.

The attention ops then drop `token_to_request`, the static `MAX_REQS = 2`
fan-out, and the cross-request `hetero_*` / `issue511_*_permutation` fixtures.
`position_ids` is **retained** as the kernel-facing per-token position input
(the #511/#512-blessed lowered form), not replaced by a `chunk_start` scalar.

This is a concrete **layering** follow-up to #382: it decides *where* the
var-len request loop lives (in the layer) and reduces the attention ops to the
degenerate single-request case that #382 calls for.

### Motivation / Use Case

- #382 mandates that B=1 be the degenerate case of the group-batch contract and
  that attention must NOT derive request/position from `t // S`. Today the
  prefill attention ops do the opposite — they internally fan over
  `MAX_REQS = 2` and resolve `req = token_to_request[t]` per token, with a large
  suite of `hetero_*` / `issue511_*_block_table_permutation` fixtures whose only
  purpose is to exercise cross-request packing inside a single 128-token tile.
- Mixing tokens from different requests inside one fixed 128-tile is an artifact
  of the current static bring-up, not a serving requirement: in practice a
  128-token prefill chunk is one request's slice; cross-request packing only
  happens at pack boundaries, which the layer handles via `cu_q_lens`.
- Concentrating batching in one place (the layer) makes the attention kernels
  simpler, removes the per-token request lookup, eliminates a whole class of
  cross-request edge fixtures, and matches the proven
  `models/qwen3/14b/prefill_fwd.py` layering.

### Proposed API / Behavior

`prefill_layer` owns batching (qwen3-style single loop):

```python
for req in range(num_reqs):                  # per-request loop (cu_q_lens)
    t0, t1 = cu_q_lens[req], cu_q_lens[req + 1]
    # slice this request's token run + its block_table row + position_ids;
    # chunk if (t1 - t0) exceeds the tile cap, cross-chunk via paged KV cache.
    attn_out[t0:t1] = prefill_attention_x(    # inlined single-request op
        q[t0:t1],
        block_table[req],                     # single request's table
        position_ids[t0:t1],                  # = context_lens[req] + local_idx
        ...,
    )
```

Attention op signature changes (all three):

```text
- token_to_request: [MAX_TOKENS]                  # REMOVED (kernel-side; stays at the layer per #512)
- block_table:      [MAX_REQS, MAX_BLOCKS]  ->  [MAX_BLOCKS]        # one request
- num_tokens (active over mixed-req T)      ->  this request's chunk length (<=128)
  position_ids:     [MAX_TOKENS]                  # RETAINED, unchanged: the #511/#512-blessed
                                                  # lowered absolute position; the layer fills it
                                                  # per request as context_lens[req] + local_idx.
                                                  # No chunk_start scalar is added: #511/#512 keep
                                                  # start_pos fixture-only and standardize on
                                                  # position_ids for RoPE / block-table lookup.
- MAX_REQS                                        # REMOVED from attention ops
```

Pipeline consistency: the sparse producers (`prefill_indexer*`,
`prefill_compressor*`) that feed attention must also be sliced/driven
per-request by the layer, so the whole CSA/HCA pipeline is single-request below
the layer boundary. `token_to_request` / `cu_q_lens` stay at the layer (the #382
contract, and #512 keeps `token_to_request` an adapter/builder field the kernel
is not forced to consume); `position_ids` remains the one position input the
attention op reads.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Target A — mirror the gitcode reference**
  (`models/deepseek_v4/sparse_compress_flash_attention_impl.py`,
  `win_attention_impl.py`): keep each attention op multi-request var-len, with
  the per-request loop INSIDE the op driven by `actual_seq_q` / `cu_seqlens_q`,
  and replace static `MAX_REQS = 2` with dynamic `cu_seqlens`. Pros: matches the
  authoritative gitcode goldens; var-len packs tiles fuller for short requests.
  Cons: every op re-implements per-request slicing; less modular for pypto-lib's
  separate-kernel bring-up structure.
- **Chosen — Target B (this issue)** = qwen3 loop placement (loop in the layer) +
  pypto-lib modular separate ops. Trade-off: single-request tiles can under-fill
  for many short requests vs. the var-len-in-op approach; acceptable for the
  current bring-up.
- **Position encoding — chunk_start scalar vs position_ids tensor**: an earlier
  draft of this issue added a `chunk_start` / `seqused_kv` scalar and derived
  `pos = chunk_start + local_idx` in-op. Dropped in favor of keeping the existing
  `position_ids[MAX_TOKENS]` tensor: #511 lists `position_ids` as shared base
  metadata "用于 RoPE、compressor boundary 判断和 block-table 查表", and #512
  standardizes the serving path on `position_ids` while keeping `start_pos`
  fixture-only. Keeping `position_ids` also matches the decode SWA/HCA/CSA ops,
  which already take `position_ids[T]`.

### Additional Context

- Precedent for Target B: `models/qwen3/14b/prefill_fwd.py` —
  `for b in pl.parallel(0, user_batch, 1)` wraps the whole layer; the attention
  scope is single-request per iteration; packed token-major
  (`T = sum(chunk_lens)`), no `[batch, max_seq]` padding.
- gitcode reference (Target A):
  `models/deepseek_v4/{sparse_compress_flash_attention_impl,win_attention_impl}.py`
  — standalone var-len ops, per-request loop inside each op, dynamic
  `batch_size_sym = seqused_kv.shape[0]`, no layer file.
- Related: #382 (packed prefill metadata contract — this issue is the layering
  decision under it), #410 (dynamic-shape refactor across decode/prefill),
  #511 / #512 (KV cache + position metadata contract that blesses `position_ids`).

### Progress

- [x] Shared `prefill_sparse_attn` (both wrappers + gather) single-request:
  drop `token_to_request`, block tables `[MAX_REQS, *] -> [*]`, drop the
  `MAX_REQS` cache-pool multiplier. Standalone PASS on a2a3.
- [x] `prefill_attention_swa` op + golden + fixtures + test single-request;
  hetero / block-table-permutation cases removed. Standalone PASS on a2a3
  (custom / suffix / issue511_active_no_write_slot).
- [ ] `prefill_attention_hca` single-request (op + fixtures + golden).
- [ ] `prefill_attention_csa` single-request (op + fixtures + golden).
- [ ] `prefill_layer` per-request loop + single-request call sites.

title: feat(deepseek/v4): gather-free split-half RoPE for the decode path (draft, decode-only)
body:
## Summary

**Draft / direction proposal — decode-only, not yet validated by the serving system.**

Converts the DeepSeek-V4 **decode** RoPE path from the interleaved (GPT-J, gather-based) layout to **split-half** (GPT-NeoX, gather-free). The rotation partner of lane `k` becomes lane `k+HALF` — a contiguous `lo=[:HALF]` / `hi=[HALF:]` slice instead of a `j^1` swap-gather.

## What

- **Forward** (`qkv_proj_rope` q+kv, `decode_compressor_ratio{4,128}`): `out_lo = x_lo*cos − x_hi*sin`, `out_hi = x_lo*sin + x_hi*cos`. The compressors fold the per-column gamma per-half (gamma does not commute with the rotation).
- **Inverse** (`decode_sparse_attn{,_hca,_swa}`): `out_lo = x_lo*cos + x_hi*sin`, `out_hi = x_hi*cos − x_lo*sin` (the conjugate of forward).
- **Callers** (`decode_attention_{hca,swa,csa}`) feed half-width FP32 `rope_cos_half` / `rope_sin_half`; `decode_layer_dp_ep` drops the interleaved-table plumbing.
- Removes the in-kernel `rope_cs` dup-gather pre-pass and all `VGATHER`s from the RoPE kernels. Net −10 lines.

## Why

The interleaved layout forces a per-element gather (`j^1` swap + `j>>1` dup) that on-device profiling showed to be the dominant RoPE cost (an earlier mask-pattern alternative measured **+61%**, confirming the gather — not the arithmetic — is the bottleneck). Split-half makes every rotation a contiguous-slice + plain FMAs, with no cross-lane op.

## Validation (a2a3, on-device)

- **Bit-exact:** HCA standalone + composed + `--layer-id 3`; SWA standalone + composed + `--layer-id 0`; CSA standalone + composed; compressors 128 + 4 standalone. The tight standalone `ratio_allclose(1e-4, 1/128)` checks discriminate sign errors (a negative-control flipped sign produced 1.59 max-abs error).
- **L2 swimlane** (HCA attention module): rope compute 2970 → 877 µs (**−70.5%**), module wall-clock 1821 → 1645 µs (**−9.6%**). Per-kernel: `q_head_rope_fused` −77%, inverse `rope` −71%, `kv_rope_fused` −69%, `rmsnorm_rope` −38%, `rope_cs` eliminated. Non-rope kernels within ±2% noise.

## Caveats (why this is a draft)

- **Decode-only.** `qkv_proj_rope` is shared with prefill; prefill's own sparse_attn / compressors stay interleaved, so prefill is **latently half-converted** — its kernel==golden tests still pass, but the output is wrong vs the true model. Prefill conversion (~10 files, same pattern) is a tracked follow-up.
- **Deployment weight-permutation.** Real checkpoints need an offline permutation of the q-proj / k_pe / `wo_a` rope columns (interleaved → split-half) to stay bit-identical to the trained model. Synthetic tests need none; this is documented but not included here.
- **Pre-existing CSA-layer fault.** `decode_layer_dp_ep --layer-id 10` (CSA, 2-device) fails with AICore `507018` — but **`main` fails identically at the same point**, so it is pre-existing and unrelated to this change.
- **Not yet validated end-to-end by the serving system.**

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Fix: dsv4 lm_head SSA tile-name collision corrupting logits accumulation
body:
## Summary

Fixes a precision break in the `lm_head` matmul. The peeled (`kb==0`) tiles and the tail accumulator shared names with the carry-loop tiles; within the inlined function scope, reusing one name across the peel and the carry loop (or across a different shape such as `VOCAB_TAIL` vs `VOCAB_CHUNK`) collides under SSA and **corrupts the matmul accumulation**, producing wrong logits.

## Changes

- Give the peel/tail tiles and the tail accumulator names distinct from the carry-loop tiles — fixes the precision break.
- Replace `pl.slice`/`pl.assemble` with native Python slice indexing in both the main vocab blocks and the tail block.
- Rename the host orchestration entry from `host_orch` to `l3_lm_head`.

Pre-commit hooks (header check, english-only, ruff) pass.

title: Refactor: align dsv4 decode/prefill numerics to golden and real-weight precision
body:
## Summary
- Align dsv4 decode attention/MoE numerics to the device-emulation golden: cast modes (RNE/rint for fp32->bf16 caches), expert_routed routing-weight fold, indexer hadamard, inverse-RoPE fp32 staging — reordering golden to match the kernel where the kernel is the perf-optimal-but-equivalent order, fixing the kernel only where golden is ground-truth (RNE cast).
- Store dsv4 decode norm weights as BF16 to match the W8A8 checkpoint (`convert_w8a8_flash.py`); apply sites cast up to FP32 per use.
- Mirror the same numeric/dtype alignment into the prefill layer and its compressors/indexer.
- Replace the synthetic `x_hc` 0.05-std init with `uniform(-1, 1)` (O(1), matching real activation magnitude). The tiny init diluted the residual and over-represented attention quant error in rel-L2; the O(1) init drops all rel-L2 dramatically (prefill SWA 5.65% -> 0.61%, decode CSA 1.08% -> 0.60%).
- Raise prefill hca/csa `x_out` `diff_thd` 3e-3 -> 5e-3: 3e-3 sits below one bf16 ULP at O(1) (2^-8 ~= 0.0039) and only counts quantization noise. Above the floor the exceedance is 0% (hca) / 0.001% (csa); the residual divergence is the causal-mask sharp-softmax sensitivity of early tokens, not a kernel bug (rel-L2 ~1.5%, cosine 0.9997).
- Tighten decode_layer / prefill_layer `x_next` `pct_thd` 0.1 -> 0.05 (synthetic frac>1e-2 <= 1.3% decode, 1.73% prefill CSA worst case) and refresh the real-weight over-thd comment tables under the new init.

## Related Issues
N/A

title: Fix dsv4 prefill_sparse_attn per-head NOPE corruption; align to decode
body:
## Summary
- Fix the DeepSeek-V4 prefill sparse-attention precision gap (much worse than
  decode): the bespoke per-block control flow (separate oi tensors, conditional
  block skips, hand-unrolled merge) corrupted the first head of each 16-head
  tile (~20% NOPE error). Replaced with decode's unified oi + unconditional
  block merge (invalid blocks die via `beta == 0`).
- Refactor `prefill_sparse_attn` to mirror `decode_sparse_attn`'s structure
  throughout: fused rope/li, single QK+PV scope (two KV views to sidestep the
  one-param-two-transpose limit #1532), unified `SPARSE_HEAD_TILE`, and the
  flattened proj_a/quant/proj_b tiling.
- Collapse gather + compute into one decode-style `prefill_sparse_attn`
  function and delete the duplicate `prefill_sparse_attn_padded_indices` entry.
- Build the softmax bias in a single vectorized `build_bias` spmd, folding the
  per-token `cmp_sparse_lens` prefix-clamp into the bias and dropping the
  `sparse_indices_eff` scratch table (a GM tensor + 128 scalar writes/token).
- Tidy constants/comments and drop the `HCA_` prefix from the re-exported
  cache-block-count constants.

Verified bit-equivalent end-to-end on a2a3 with real W8A8 weights: standalone
attn_out rel-L2 0.077%/0.085%/0.065% (ratio 0/4/128); prefill_layer x_next
swa(L0) 0.24%, hca(L9) 0.70%, csa(L8) 0.82%.

title: feat(deepseek/v4): gather-free split-half RoPE for decode + prefill
body:
## Summary

Converts the DeepSeek-V4 RoPE path from the interleaved (GPT-J, gather-based) layout to split-half (GPT-NeoX, gather-free) for **both decode and prefill**, so the whole chain is layout-consistent. The rotation partner of lane `k` becomes lane `k+HALF` — a contiguous `lo=[:HALF]`/`hi=[HALF:]` slice instead of a `j^1` swap-gather + `j>>1` cos/sin dup-gather. Every RoPE rotation becomes contiguous slices + plain FMAs, with no cross-lane op and no in-kernel `rope_cs` dup-gather pre-pass.

- **Decode** (commit 1): adopts the split-half conversion across `qkv_proj_rope` (forward, shared), `decode_compressor_ratio{4,128}` (forward), and `decode_sparse_attn{,_hca,_swa}` (inverse), with the callers feeding half-width FP32 `rope_cos_half`/`rope_sin_half`. Two precision details vs current `main`: the compressor `gamma_rope` is kept cast to FP32 (since `norm_w` is BF16), and the inverse-rope stage (already FP32) is read directly — no FP32→FP32 identity cast.
- **Prefill** (commit 2): mirrors the same conversion onto `prefill_compressor_ratio{4,128}` (forward) and `prefill_sparse_attn` (inverse), with `prefill_attention_{csa,hca,swa}` building and passing the half-width tables. This removes the latent "half-converted" hazard from converting the shared `qkv_proj_rope` without converting prefill's own compressors/inverse. Rebased on top of #569 — its per-head NOPE fix and the `prefill_sparse_attn_padded_indices` removal are preserved.

Forward: `out_lo = x_lo*cos − x_hi*sin`, `out_hi = x_lo*sin + x_hi*cos`. Inverse (conjugate): `out_lo = x_lo*cos + x_hi*sin`, `out_hi = x_hi*cos − x_lo*sin`.

The lightning **indexer** (`{decode,prefill}_indexer{,_compressor}`) is intentionally left interleaved: it is a self-contained RoPE subsystem (own query/KV rope from the freqs tables) that feeds sparse attention only integer top-k indices, so it is decoupled from the main path.

### Why

On-device profiling showed the per-element gather (`j^1` swap + `j>>1` dup) — not the arithmetic — is the dominant RoPE cost. The earlier interleaved L2 swimlane on the HCA attention module measured rope compute 2970 → 877 µs (**−70.5%**) and module wall-clock −9.6% from this change.

### Validation (a2a3sim, golden, all PASS)

`decode_compressor_ratio4/128`, `decode_sparse_attn{,_hca,_swa}`, `qkv_proj_rope`, `decode_attention_{csa,hca,swa}`, `decode_layer`; `prefill_compressor_ratio4/128`, `prefill_sparse_attn`, `prefill_attention_{csa,hca,swa}`, `prefill_layer`. The `*_sparse_attn_swa` standalone test is occasionally flaky (~4/6) but identically so on `main` (unseeded fixtures from #563 against a tight tolerance) — not introduced by this change.

### Caveat

Real checkpoints need an offline interleaved→split-half permutation of the trained `q-proj`/`k_pe`/`wo_a` rope columns to stay bit-identical to the trained model. Synthetic tests need none. Not yet validated on-device or end-to-end by the serving system.

## Related Issues

- Builds on / supersedes #564 (decode-only draft) by completing the prefill conversion.
- Rebased onto #569 (prefill_sparse_attn NOPE fix), which it preserves.

title: perf(dsv4 decode): gather_kv staging coalesce + rebalance (~-1.6% L2 wall)
body:
## Summary

Three changes to the DeepSeek-V4 unified decode layer (`models/deepseek/v4/decode_sparse_attn.py` + the insight export tool), rebased on the current upstream main (post #568 numerics-align and #569 prefill fix):

1. **perf(gather_kv): coalesce dead-store + rebalance compressed staging** — the measurable win. The compressed-cache gather stages each `GATHER_FILL_TILE` block in a UB tile (one row per scattered load, so loads stream on MTE2 with no buffer-reuse WAR) and flushes it with a single wide MTE3 store instead of many 1-row stores; the window pass drops its now-dead bulk-zero of the `[WIN, PADDED_TOPK)` region (the block stores fully rewrite it). The compressed gather also runs as a finer `T * N_CMP_BLK` SPMD so it fills the AIV cores more evenly across waves.
2. **perf(vector micro-ops)** — below-noise cleanups: 2-op `sparse_bias` (`min(idx, 0) * -NEG_INF` vs the add/max/min/sub clamp chain) and `col_expand_add` of the per-block softmax bias (dropping a dead `pl.full(0)` base + a separate add).
3. **tools(export_all_kernel_insight)** — orphan-safe msprof teardown + a `--max-time 0` default, so the per-kernel insight sweep is not truncated (and does not leak an orphaned sim) under task-submit's 300s cap.

## Performance

a2a3, real device, L2-swimlane total wall (µs), 2 A/B samples each (this branch vs the same kernel reverted to upstream main):

| sample | upstream main | this branch | gain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1548.0 | 1522.3 | -1.67% |
| 2 | 1527.7 | 1505.6 | -1.45% |
| mean | 1537.9 | 1513.9 | **-1.56%** |

Below the ±3% single-run noise floor, but stable in sign and magnitude across 4 measurements (these two + the -1.78% originally measured for the gather change). The micro-ops contribute negligibly; the gain is the gather restructuring.

## Testing

- `decode_sparse_attn.py` golden PASSES on a2a3 (CSA path), on the upstream-rebased kernel.

title: Refactor: clean up dsv4 prefill imports to match decode standard
body:
## Summary
- Align dsv4 prefill module imports to the decode reference: `config` is the constants leaf each module derives from locally, and cross-module imports carry only kernel/golden **functions**, never constants or `*`.
- Drop `from decode_* import *` star imports in `prefill_compressor_ratio4`, `prefill_indexer_compressor`, `prefill_indexer`, `prefill_attention_csa`; replace with explicit config-derived headers mirroring the matching decode module (incl. previously star-hidden names `HEAD_TILE`, `CSA_TOPK_TOKEN_TILE`).

- Keep only the forward function imports from `prefill_sparse_attn` (`prefill_sparse_attn`, `golden_prefill_sparse_attn`, `_quant_w_per_channel`) in the attention wrappers, matching decode's `from decode_sparse_attn import sparse_attn`.
- Remove the now-unnecessary `# ruff: noqa: F401,F403,F405,F821` blanket suppressions that only existed for the star imports.

Pure import/constant relocation — all derived values are identical to before. ruff clean; all seven standalone modules pass on a2a3 NPU; real-weight `prefill_layer` validation (swa/hca/csa, cards 14,15) shows the x_next error distribution unchanged (rel-L2 0.24% / 0.70% / 0.82%, cosine ≥ 0.99979).

title: docs: precision-tuning guide + golden error_distribution; fold dynamic-shape into coding-style
body:
## Summary

Documentation + a small golden-harness addition capturing the precision lessons from the recent DeepSeek-V4 work, plus a coding-style consolidation.

- **New `docs/precision-tuning.md`** — keeping a kernel numerically faithful to its torch reference:
  - `pl.cast` rounding-mode table vs torch-CPU (default `round` is ties-away; torch `.to()` is RNE → use `rint`)
  - kernel/golden implementation parity (identical op order *and* dtype at each step)
  - input/output dtype alignment; fp32 intermediates and no double-cast (`fp32→int8`, never via bf16)
  - quantization-scheme choices; the `error_distribution` threshold sweep; dump-based stage localization; real-weight testing
- **`golden.error_distribution`** — a reusable diagnostic comparator (promoted from the prefill-layer `measuring()` helper): prints rel-L2 / cosine, a `frac>thd` table, and rel/abs/golden-magnitude percentiles. Always passes (measurement, not a gate); exported from `golden`.
- **`docs/pypto-coding-style.md`** — two new sections:
  - §7 Dynamic Shapes (condensed from the now-deleted `dynamic-shape-guidelines.md`)
  - §8 naming/comment conventions (name tile sizes, inline block counts; comments state *what*, not *why* except unresolved-issue references; no `Stage 1:`/`Loop A:` narration)
- **`docs/dynamic-shape-guidelines.md` deleted** (folded into coding-style §7).
- **`docs/debugging.md`** — cross-references precision-tuning and drops the duplicated precision-localization steps (now in precision-tuning §7).
- **README / CLAUDE.md** — index the new doc; order debugging before the tuning docs.

## Testing

- `golden.error_distribution` smoke-tested (bf16-rounding input → expected rel-L2 / frac>thd / percentile report).
- Pre-commit hooks pass: check-headers, check-english-only, ruff.
- Docs-only otherwise; no kernel behavior changes.

title: docs: add in-core kernel profiling skill and guide
body:
## What

Port the **incore-profiling** skill into pypto-lib and document it. The skill runs cycle-accurate, single-AI-core profiling of every PTOAS kernel in a build via the Ascend `msprof op simulator`, then collects MindStudio Insight traces.

## Changes

- **`.claude/skills/incore-profiling/`** — standalone `.pto`-driven profiler. For each kernel it generates a single-core simulator testcase (`gen_profiling_case.py` reads the kernel signature + sibling `.pto` shapes), builds it, runs it on the op-simulator, and collects the trace. No model run and no PTOAS checkout required; CANN / SoC / arch auto-resolved from `--target`, with preflight for TL-capable bisheng and auto-provisioning of a missing `msopprof` worker.
- **`docs/incore-profiling.md`** — pypto-lib usage guide: prerequisites (wq3 env, ptoas-bin), `task-submit` invocation with `--cann-set-env`, output layout, the `clean_sim_trace` step for Perfetto, the data-dependent-kernel caveat, and a troubleshooting table. Positioned as the L0 / instruction-level drill-down for `performance-tuning.md` Part 2.
- **`docs/performance-tuning.md`** — link Part 2 to the new guide.

- Relationship to the existing `tools/export_all_kernel_insight.py` / `--export-kernel-insight` is documented in the guide (the skill is the ad-hoc, single-kernel path that needs no model run).
