title: perf(dsv4/csa): cut decode CSA task count and dependency latency
body:
## Summary

Perf pass over the DeepSeek-V4 decode CSA path (indexer, qkv, MoE), reducing task count, shortening the critical path, and letting the scheduler dispatch it first.

**Indexer**
- Fold the nope bf16 cast into `qr_rope` and collapse the Hadamard rotation to a single matmul.
- Split `qr_hadamard_quant` into separate cube and vector scopes.
- Split `weights_proj` over K rather than N (26us -> 10.7us in `decode_layer`).
- Double the inner compressor's `kv_score_proj` task count.
- Mark the decode spmd chain `allow_early_resolve`, and close the remaining early-resolve gaps on the critical path.

**QKV**
- Halve the `q_head_rms_nope_rope` task count (4 heads per task).

**Dependency scheduling**
- `rms_norm` fans out to `qr_proj_matmul` (critical path), `kv_proj_matmul`, both compressors' `kv_score_proj`, and `weights_proj`, which all become ready the instant it retires and race for the cores. Hang a `pl.system.task_dummy` barrier off the `rms_norm` TaskId and route the four off-critical-path consumers through it, so `qr_proj_matmul` is dispatched first. The auto-tracked edges on `x_normed` are unchanged; the dummy edge is just strictly later. This requires `rms_norm` to switch to the `with pl.spmd(...) as tid` capture form (the `for ... in pl.spmd(N)` form yields no TaskId) and to return that tid instead of `x_normed`, which no caller consumed. Standalone test wrappers, which have no `rms_norm` producer, pass `task_dummy(deps=[])` (pypto #1987).

**MoE**
- Split the routed expert gate/up matmuls into their own parallel nest.

Validated on a2a3: `qkv_proj_rope`, `decode_indexer`, `decode_indexer_compressor`, `decode_compressor_ratio4`, `decode_attention_csa`, and `decode_layer` (ep2) all PASS. Note `decode_attention_csa` fails on `a2a3sim` both before and after this branch (known sparse-attn simulator issue); real hardware passes.

## Related Issues

None.

title: fix(dsv4): make prefill HC post active-token aware
body:
## Summary

- Add `hc_post_active(...)` for prefill: HC post-mixing is scheduled only for rows below `num_tokens`.
- Fill the remaining static `T=128` tail with deterministic FP32 zeros using coarse 16-token tiles.
- Use the active-aware helper at the SWA, HCA, and CSA attention exits while leaving decode and MoE/FFN `hc_post` paths unchanged.
- Align the three attention goldens with the zero-tail output contract.
- Limit the ratio-4 main and indexer-compressor softmax-pool grids to the maximum number of compressed rows reachable by the active token prefix.

## Root Cause

Prefill tensors are statically allocated for 128 tokens. A poison-tail component probe showed that HC pre/post math is row-local: changing inactive residual rows does not change any active output (`active_delta=0`). However, the existing full-T `hc_post` mixes and writes those inactive residual rows into the layer output, so stale tail values persist across the 43-layer graph.

The previous input-side workaround materialized an 8 MiB FP32 HC tensor before every attention, copied active rows, zeroed the tail, and still ran full-T `hc_post`. This patch fixes the producer that establishes the next layer boundary instead:

- active rows execute the original HC post math unchanged;
- inactive rows execute no HC math and receive padding only;
- no extra full-T HC input tensor is materialized.

The extended boundary matrix exposed a second partial-token issue. The ratio-4 main and inner indexer compressors always launched their full 64/128-block pooling grids. With `num_tokens=17`, only 4-5 compressed rows are reachable, leaving most pool blocks inactive. In the 43-layer EP8 graph, some ranks stalled in `prefill_c4_softmax_pool` or `prefill_idx_c4_softmax_pool`; other ranks then surfaced as stuck in the following MoE dispatch barrier. Raising the scheduler timeout to 320 seconds did not change the failure point.

The compressor fix uses `ceil(num_tokens / COMPRESS_RATIO) * HEAD_BLOCKS` as the grid upper bound. This is safe for the current contiguous active-prefix contract and arbitrary start-position alignment. For 17 tokens, the main/inner grids fall from 64/128 blocks to 10/20; the 128-token grids are unchanged.

## Controlled Performance Check

For `num_tokens=4`, a single component graph ran the old guarded path and the new active path on the same input:

| Path | Task/block count | Aggregate AIV exec |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| input guard + full `hc_post` | 256 | 2.129 ms |
| active `hc_post` + tail fill | 36 | 1.116 ms |

This reduces related task/block count by 85.9% and aggregate AIV execution by 47.6%. The component swimlane was generated from build `_jit_inactive_hc_probe_20260710_101350`.

## Files

- `models/deepseek/v4/hc_post.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_attention_swa.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_attention_hca.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_attention_csa.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_compressor_ratio4.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_indexer_compressor.py`

Debug probes are intentionally excluded from the PR.

## Validation

- `python3 -m py_compile` for all changed modules: PASS
- `git diff --check`: PASS
- HC post boundary/poison-tail matrix: 39/39 PASS
- SWA/HCA/CSA active-token and suffix matrix: all valid cases PASS; inactive output tails are exactly zero
- Ratio-4 boundary correctness:
  - CSA `start_pos=0,num_tokens=1`: PASS
  - CSA `start_pos=3,num_tokens=1`: PASS
  - CSA `start_pos=100,num_tokens=50`: PASS
  - main/indexer compressor standalone `start_pos=3`: PASS
- EP2, 43-layer prefill: `num_tokens=17` PASS, build `_jit_l3_prefill_fwd_20260711_102831`, runtime 104.29 s
- EP8, 43-layer prefill:

| `num_tokens` | Build | Runtime | Result |
| ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | `_jit_l3_prefill_fwd_20260710_095133` | 318.81 s | PASS |
| 2 | `_jit_l3_prefill_fwd_20260710_100220` | 326.42 s | PASS |
| 8 | `_jit_l3_prefill_fwd_20260710_102722` | 326.98 s | PASS |
| 17 | `_jit_l3_prefill_fwd_20260711_101801` | 316.78 s | PASS |
| 32 | `_jit_l3_prefill_fwd_20260711_103547` | 324.52 s | PASS |
| 33 | `_jit_l3_prefill_fwd_20260711_104642` | 311.31 s | PASS |
| 63 | `_jit_l3_prefill_fwd_20260711_105733` | 304.19 s | PASS |
| 128 | `_jit_l3_prefill_fwd_20260710_103818` | 304.90 s | PASS |

Each newly added EP8 boundary value was compiled independently because `num_tokens` is statically specialized in the current build. The full-forward driver is kernel-only and has no golden function; module-level correctness and exact tail padding are covered by the standalone attention/compressor tests and poison-tail probe.

title: [Feature] Add serving contract support for lib-serving decoupling
body:
### Summary

Add a pypto-lib owned serving contract layer so pypto-serving can consume model kernel ABI details through structured contracts instead of duplicating lib internals.

### Motivation / Use Case

The serving-side architecture work is tracked in hw-native-sys/pypto-serving#65. To complete the decoupling, pypto-lib should become the source of truth for model-specific serving ABI details, including kernel loading, host-side JIT wrapper signatures, compile/runtime argument builders, weight layout preparation, and compatibility validation.

This keeps pypto-serving focused on runtime orchestration while allowing Qwen3-14B, DeepSeek-V4 Flash/Pro, and future models to expose their serving requirements through lib-owned contracts.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Introduce pypto-lib support for:

- a serving contract registry that selects a `ModelServingContract` from explicit family/variant or structured model config metadata;
- `ModelServingContract` metadata for model identity, capabilities, limits, KV/cache layout, execution graph, kernel specs, and weight metadata;
- lib-owned kernel loaders and validators;
- lib-owned host-side JIT wrappers, compile argument builders, runtime argument builders, and weight layout preparation hooks;
- structured compatibility errors including schema version, ABI fingerprint, incompatible field, and suggested action.

Detailed design reference: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-serving/issues/65

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

title: Fix: restore Qwen3 prefill ring isolation
body:
## Summary

- Restore the Qwen3-14B prefill runtime-scope topology used before the
  fused QKPV rewrite: parent token scope, one RoPE/KV scope, and one
  attention scope per finalization window.
- Keep `all_q_padded_tile` and `attn_tile` in the parent token scope so
  they bridge child scopes without retaining child scratch tensors.
- Keep `attn_tile` as an inout buffer instead of returning and rebinding

title: Add direct CANN FAI decode attention for Qwen3
body:
## Summary
- Replace Qwen3-14B decode attention with a direct mixed CCEC kernel derived from CANN `FusedInferAttentionScore` and invoked through `pl.jit.extern`.
- Preserve the serving ABI and vLLM physical layouts: active TND query/output and paged BSND KV cache. KV reshaping is a zero-copy view inside the compiled graph; no cache layout conversion is materialized.
- Select the 19-core flash-decode path for long B1 attention and the 24-core regular path for true B16 and short B1 through runtime tiling.
- Support runtime execution on A2/A3 for active batches 1 and 16 only. A2/A3 simulation is compile-only; B2-B15 and A5 are explicitly unsupported.
- Declare cache layout, supported batches, and runtime/compile platforms in the Qwen3 contract.
- Adapt prefill cache writes to BSND while preserving the four manual scopes from #753.
- Vendor and attribute the required CANN kernel subset. The external mixed-kernel and `include_dirs` support are available in merged PyPTO #2009.
- Keep the HOST tuple return compatible with current PyPTO specialization and run the B16/4096-token serving warmup with the 2 GiB ring capacity validated by #753.

## Testing
- `python -m pytest -q tests/golden tests/contract`: 189 passed.
- `decode_fwd.py -p a2a3sim --smoke`: all 37 generated functions compiled.
- Current PyPTO `b2f347f` compiled the complete serving HOST decode wrapper to `DistributedCompiledProgram`.
- A2/A3 hardware correctness passed at sequence length 3338 for B1 and true B16 with independent paged KV ranges.
- Hardware CI-shape accuracy with 2 GiB heap and 16K task/dep pools passed under `task-submit` task `task_20260713_013155_194847010745`.
- Full serving hardware golden passed all 8 expected tokens through pypto-serving #69.
- True B16 serving with 16 distinct prompts matched 16 independent B1 references.
- A 3338-token, 40-layer B1 serving run completed 19 decode steps without device deadlock. Decode TPOT was 31.2 ms, kernel wall average was 30.82 ms, and device Effective was 28.53 ms.
- L2 timing at the same B1 shape measured a 42.39 us median slowest-AIV span inside the mixed launch and a 166.12 us median scheduler-visible attention stage from tiler dispatch through mixed completion. These are intentionally reported as different timing boundaries.

## Compatibility
- Requires pypto-serving #69 for active B1/B16 dispatch and early rejection of unsupported runtime shapes.

## Merge order
1. Squash-merge this PR first. Its required checks and all kernel checks pass.
2. Update pypto-serving #69's submodule to the resulting squash SHA.
3. Rerun and merge pypto-serving #69.

The non-required serving check currently fails before NPU execution because it intentionally tests pypto-serving main, whose old HOST tuple wrapper is incompatible with current PyPTO specialization. The companion fix and full hardware validation are in pypto-serving #69.

title: perf(qwen3-14b decode): reapply the fa_fused fusion (#656 + #682), reverted by #703
body:
Reapplies the Qwen3-14B decode **fusion** commits that pypto-lib#703 reverted.

> **Rebased onto current `main`.** #747 (`Restore "Refactor Qwen3 decode forward path (#670)"`)
> has since re-landed the #670 refactor, so this PR no longer carries it — #670 is now
> part of the base. What remains is exactly the fusion, which #747 did **not** restore.

| commit | author | what |
|---|---|---|
| `0e3d05b` | Siyuan Feng | #656 — fuse rope+attn+softmax into one `fa_fused` kernel |
| `22b5dfb` | lyfne123 | #682 — funnel MLP/out seed successors through `fa_fused` |
| `5885235` | — | `sync_start=True` on the `fa_fused` spmd |

The first two are the reverted commits **reapplied verbatim** — not one byte changed,
original authorship intact. Everything this PR does differently from the original lands
in the last commit, so the delta is reviewable on its own.

Net change against `main` is **one file**: `models/qwen3/14b/decode_fwd.py` (287+/287−).

## Why it was reverted, and why it is safe now

The fusion was **correct all along**. It broke only because it happened to step on
**three** silent-data-corruption bugs in pypto — each compiles clean, raises nothing,
produces no NaN:

| issue | status | defect | drop it and this kernel emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| pypto#2003 | ✅ fixed | a Group wrapper forwarding a multi-result call's tuple poisons the return-param map; codegen falls back to tail-alignment and binds a consumer to the **wrong tensor** | ` atext有关` |
| pypto#2007 | ✅ fixed | `tile.concat` missing `.not_inplace_safe()` → MemoryReuse aliases dst onto a src, and tconcat is a *shifted* copy, so it clobbers the source before reading it | ` a leading company in the` |
| pypto#2010 | ✅ fixed | `t[:, a:b]` on a **multi-row** tile: `TEXTRACT` repacks strided→dense **over its own live source**. `ROWS == 1` is safe — which is exactly why the K path (row-sliced to 1 row first) worked and the 16-row Q path was destroyed | ` a leading company in the` |

**All three fixes are now on pypto `main`** — `12fd445` (#2004), `ba0ace8` (#2008) and
`018178d` (#2011) respectively — so this PR is no longer blocked. pypto-lib's CI does not
pin pypto (`setup-sim-job` syncs the clone to `origin HEAD` on every run), so CI builds
against a pypto that carries all three. With them, the kernel needs no changes beyond
`sync_start=True`.

Established by a leave-one-out ablation: five pypto builds (all three fixes, and each
one dropped in turn), the same kernel tree on each, judged by real generated tokens for
the prompt "Huawei is" (correct: `a Chinese multinational technology company` /
`[264, 8453, 67926, 5440, 2813]`). Dropping any of the three yields wrong tokens —
note that #2007's and #2010's are *fluent English*, which is why this class of bug
survived for months.

**pypto#2006 (`pl.split_aiv(2, NONE)` drops one AIV lane's writeback) is NOT a
dependency of this PR.** It is a real pypto defect — its standalone reproducer loses
64 of 128 items without the fix and passes with it — but this kernel does not trigger
it: dropping that fix leaves the generated tokens byte-identical to the correct output
and the logit error at the reference's own noise floor (0.064 @ seq_len=6, argmax
16/16). It should still be fixed in pypto; it just does not gate this PR.

## Resolved since the first revision of this PR

Two things this PR previously had to carry are now handled upstream by #747, and are
gone from the diff:

- **`greedy_sample.py`.** #670 originally deleted it, which broke serving's *prefill*
  path (pypto-serving#47 made prefill load `greedy_sample.py` by filename and dispatch
  `greedy_sample_fwd` for the first generated token; `decode_fwd`'s in-kernel sampler
  only runs at the end of a *decode* step). #747's restore keeps the file, so the
  compensating commit this PR used to carry is now redundant and has been dropped.
  `token_embed.py` and `qwen3_14b_l3_generate.py` remain removed, as intended.
- **The lock-step pypto-serving change.** The `decode_layer` → `decode_fwd` rename
  landed with #747, so serving already accepts the new module name. This PR no longer
  renames anything and needs no companion serving change.

## Verification

Measured against the **un-fused** kernel — a different kernel that passes the serving
e2e, so not a shared-code-path golden — on a fixture where every batch row shares one
`seq_len` (the serving regime). Built on a pypto carrying the three required fixes.

| seq_len | reference's own run-to-run noise | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| **6** (a real serving prompt) | 0.0555 · 16/16 | **0.0627 · 16/16** |
| 12 | 0.0377 · 16/16 | 0.0377 · 16/16 |
| 31 | 0.0248 · 16/16 | 0.0275 · 16/16 |
| 128 | 0.0101 · 16/16 | 0.0192 · 16/16 |

The error is at the reference's own noise floor and **argmax agrees 16/16 at every
length**. Before the pypto fixes this was `err@6 = 1.65`, argmax 11/16.

- **serving e2e** (`tests/test_qwen3_accuracy.py`): **passed twice** — 91.9 s, 87.7 s.
- **Token output** (`npu_generate.py`, prompt "Huawei is"): `a Chinese multinational
  technology company` / `[264, 8453, 67926, 5440, 2813]` — byte-identical to the output
  #703 quotes as correct.
- **Performance** (`PYPTO_BENCH=1`, 100 rounds, 3 reps × 3 arms interleaved in one
  device lock; intra-arm spread 102–156 µs):

  | arm | min | median |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | un-fused baseline | 36441 µs | 38772 µs |
  | + #656 + #682 | 35658 µs | 37563 µs |
  | **this PR** | **35628 µs (−2.23 %)** | **37436 µs (−3.45 %)** |

  The win is the fusion. This bench was taken before #747, so its baseline arm predates
  the #670 refactor that is now in `main`; #670's own contribution measured −30 µs min
  (inside the noise), so the speedup attributable to this PR against today's `main` is
  unchanged.

## Rebase note

`decode_fwd.py` after the rebase is **byte-identical** to the pre-rebase branch tip —
the fusion is preserved exactly. `tests/golden/test_qwen3_greedy_source.py` passes
against `main`'s version of the test (3/3), i.e. the fused kernel satisfies the greedy
sampling assertions without the test edit this PR used to carry.

The tip commit was re-pushed (identical tree) to start a CI run on a pypto that includes
`018178d` — the previous run had cloned pypto 32 s before that fix landed.

title: feat(tools): add L2-swimlane critical-path analysis
body:
## Summary

Add `tools/critical_path.py`, a post-processing tool that reconstructs the
critical path of an L2-swimlane run and writes a per-task compute/stall report.

- Auto-discovers every rank/device under a `build_output/<case>` directory
  (`dfx_outputs/rank*/d*/`) from `l2_swimlane_records.json` + `deps.json` +
  `name_map.json`.
- Builds a happens-before DAG from the dependency graph oriented by observed
  swimlane timestamps (keep `pred->succ` only when `end[pred] <= start[succ]`),
  then computes two critical paths:
  - **Static CPM** — longest duration-weighted path, i.e. the dependency-limited
    latency floor (unlimited cores).
  - **Observed** — the as-executed backward "blame" walk from the last-finishing
    task; each task's compute plus the runtime-scheduling stall before it
    (`data-wait` = waiting on a producer, `core-wait` = waiting for a core to be
    freed) tile the makespan exactly.
- Writes `critical_path_report.md` into the build directory: an overview
  (makespan, CPM floor, compute vs. stall split), a per-kernel-family table,
  and a full per-task listing giving each task's duration, contributed compute,
  and stall as a fraction of the makespan.
- Documents CLI usage and options in `tools/README.md`.
- Pure post-processing (no C++, no device); complexity is O(N log N).

**Usage**

```bash
# Analyze a case build produced with --enable-l2-swimlane
python tools/critical_path.py build_output/_jit_l3_decode_fwd_<timestamp>

# Options: report filename, kernel-family rows, tick tolerance, echo summary
python tools/critical_path.py build_output/<case> \
    --report critical_path_report.md --top 25 --stdout
```

It auto-discovers all ranks, so you can equally point it at a single
`dfx_outputs/rank0/d0` directory or at the whole `build_output/` tree.

**Example** (2-card DeepSeek-V4 `decode_fwd`):

```
$ python tools/critical_path.py build_output/_jit_l3_decode_fwd_20260710_014612
Analyzed 2 rank(s) under .../build_output/_jit_l3_decode_fwd_20260710_014612
[dfx_outputs/rank0/d0] makespan=59.863ms  CPM=28.84ms(48%)  compute=82.1%  stall=17.9% (core-wait 10.1%, data-wait 7.7%)
[dfx_outputs/rank1/d0] makespan=62.183ms  CPM=26.45ms(43%)  compute=75.3%  stall=24.7% (data-wait 15.1%, core-wait 9.6%)
Report written to: .../build_output/_jit_l3_decode_fwd_20260710_014612/critical_path_report.md
```

The report then breaks down, task by task, how much of the makespan is compute
on the critical path versus waiting on runtime scheduling — for this run the
static dependency floor is only ~48% of the makespan, i.e. the run is
resource/schedule-bound rather than dependency-bound, and the MoE expert GEMMs
(`exp_up/gate/w2_mm`) dominate the critical-path compute.

## Related Issues

None.

title: Update: phase-major fused MLP (Route B, M=128) in Qwen3-14B prefill
body:
## Summary
- Restructure the Qwen3-14B prefill layer into two phases so the MLP weights (~178MB each) stream from HBM once instead of per-token-block: phase 1 runs the per-tok attention path through post-attn RMSNorm and stores its two hand-offs (post_norm, first residual) for the whole packed token dim; phase 2 runs gate/up/down as flat, band-grouped token-tile sweeps.
- Tile the MLP weight matmuls at M=128 (two 64-token tiles at once) so each w_gate/w_up/w_down slab is reused across 128 rows in L1/L0, halving weight re-streaming vs the M=64 layout.
- Fully fuse gate -> up -> silu -> down per band and atomic-add each band's down partial into a residual-seeded FP32 accumulator (manual_dep=True; only seed -> down and down -> cast pinned with explicit TASK_ID deps, so both bands' atomic-adds run concurrently).
- Merge gate/up into one spmd(24) with a core-shift so the heavy-core sets are disjoint and no core exceeds 3 N-tiles.
- Bump cube K/N tiles to 256 (bf16 = 512B L2 cache line) to fix the sub-line MTE2 over-fetch that left the proj matmuls MTE2-bound; decouple the UB-bound vector epilogues (silu, down+resid) to a finer 64/128 frag.
- Preserve the upstream cross-tok-block QKV dep chaining (qkv_prev_tids) at the end of phase-1's per-tok-block scope.
- --enable-l2-swimlane now takes an int mode (0-4) instead of a boolean flag.

## Performance
Prefill wall time (b=1, 128 seq, 4 layers):
- 8600us baseline -> 6400us (-26%) with the 512B-contiguous matmul tiling (K/N tiles to 256, fills the L2 cache line).
- 6400us -> 5800us (-9%, -33% cumulative) with the phase-major fused per-band MLP + phase reorder.

Validated on NPU device: golden `out` PASS for both swimlane 0 and swimlane 1.

title: Optimize Qwen3 A8W8 decode attention scheduling
body:
## Summary

This PR optimizes the Qwen3-14B A8W8 fused decode attention path by increasing FA work granularity and reducing long-tail latency in the paged attention stage.

The change is intentionally scoped to one file:

- `models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer_a8w8.py`

It does not change the model math, checkpoint format, public serving API, prefill path, or BF16 Qwen3-14B kernels.

## Background

After the Qwen3-14B A8W8 path was brought up, decode TPOT was dominated by the attention / FA section. Profiling and 48-token generation experiments showed that the previous decode attention scheduling left too much work grouped into coarse FA tasks:

- attention tiles were relatively large (`ATTN_TILE = 64`)
- all KV heads were effectively grouped together (`GP_SIZE = 8`)
- the FA work table was encoded only by `(batch, attention_part)`
- online softmax had to infer its work base from batch-level sequencing

That shape worked functionally, but it created uneven FA work distribution and longer tail latency per decode step.

## What Changed

### 1. Split attention into smaller context tiles

`ATTN_TILE` is changed from `64` to `16`.

This makes each FA task smaller and gives the scheduler more independent work items. The goal is not to change attention semantics, but to reduce per-task tail latency and improve load balance across decode steps.

### 2. Split FA work by KV head group

`GP_SIZE` is changed from `8` to `1`, and `HEAD_GROUPS` is introduced:

```python
HEAD_GROUPS = NUM_KV_HEADS // GP_SIZE
```

The FA work-table capacity now accounts for batch, head group, and attention part:

```python
FA_TABLE_CAP = BATCH * HEAD_GROUPS * MAX_ATTN_PARTS
```

The FA work item encoding is changed from batch-only grouping to batch + head-group grouping:

```python
work_id = (wb * HEAD_GROUPS + whg) * MAX_ATTN_PARTS + wp
```

This exposes more independent FA tasks to the runtime and avoids processing all KV heads as one coarse group.

### 3. Align online softmax with the new FA work encoding

Online softmax now derives the FA completion base directly from `(batch, head_group)`:

```python
os_hg = os_gi // GP_SIZE
os_w_base = (os_b * HEAD_GROUPS + os_hg) * MAX_ATTN_PARTS
```

This keeps `fa_done`, `all_oi_tmp`, `all_cur_mi`, and `all_cur_li` aligned with the new FA task layout.

### 4. Move QK/V normalization loops to SPMD form

The QK norm and V norm loops are changed from `pl.parallel + pl.at(...)` wrappers to named `pl.spmd(...)` loops:

- `qk_norm`
- `v_norm`

This keeps the scheduling structure closer to the rest of the decode pipeline and makes task boundaries explicit.

### 5. Enable FA scheduling hints

The FA fused loop now uses:

```python
sync_start=True
allow_early_resolve=True
```

These hints are used to reduce scheduling wait and dependency tail in the fine-grained FA stage.

## Why This Helps

The optimization improves TPOT by reducing FA long-tail latency rather than by changing arithmetic.

The previous path had fewer, heavier FA tasks. With smaller attention tiles and per-head-group work-table entries, the runtime sees more independent work and can distribute decode attention more evenly. The online softmax dependency lookup is also made direct for the new work-table layout.

In short:

- more FA work items
- smaller FA task body
- better head-group-level load balance
- simpler FA completion indexing for online softmax
- no intended numerical behavior change

## Ablation Result

A same-device 48-token ablation was run with the current PR patch and with this single-file patch temporarily reverted.

Prompt:

```text
介绍一下北京故宫
```

Configuration:

- model format: `qwen3-a8w8`
- decode backend: A8W8 fused decode
- max sequence length: `512`
- generated tokens: `48`
- temperature: `0`
- top-p: `1`

Result:

| Variant | TTFT | Decode Time | Decode Steps | TPOT | Output Quality |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| PR patch enabled | 7.224s | 2.599s | 47 | **55.3 ms/token** | normal Chinese continuation |
| Patch reverted | 7.082s | 3.202s | 47 | **68.1 ms/token** | normal Chinese continuation |

TPOT improvement:

```text
(68.1 - 55.3) / 68.1 = 18.8%
```

Generated text from the PR patch run:

```text
的建筑风格和历史背景。
北京故宫，又称紫禁城，是明清两代的皇家宫殿，位于北京市中心，是世界上现存规模最大、保存最完整的古代宫殿建筑群之一。故宫的建筑风格融合了中国古代
```

Both variants produced the same token sequence for this 48-token prompt, so the measured speedup is not coming from an output-quality tradeoff.

## Additional Validation

Static checks:

```bash
python -m py_compile models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer_a8w8.py
git diff --check
```

Quick hardware smoke test:

- prompt: `介绍一下北京故宫`
- generated tokens: `8`
- output:

```text
的建筑风格和历史背景。
北京
```

- task exit code: `0`

## MAX_SEQ Scratch-Memory Validation

The finer FA partition increases the five decode-attention scratch/work tensors. With the fixed kernel shape `BATCH=16`, `NUM_KV_HEADS=8`, `HEAD_DIM=128`, and `Q_HEAD_PAD=16`, the exact allocation change is:

| `MAX_SEQ` | Previous layout | This PR | Increase |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 8.126 MiB | 32.531 MiB | +24.405 MiB |
| 4096 | 65.008 MiB | 260.250 MiB | +195.242 MiB |

At the production `MAX_SEQ=4096` setting, the breakdown is:

- `all_oi_tmp`: 64 MiB -> 256 MiB
- `all_cur_mi`: 0.5 MiB -> 2 MiB
- `all_cur_li`: 0.5 MiB -> 2 MiB
- `fa_work_table`: 4 KiB -> 128 KiB
- `fa_done`: 4 KiB -> 128 KiB

The dominant increase is therefore `all_oi_tmp`, not the work-table metadata.

A full-shape hardware run was executed with `BATCH=16`, `PTO2_MANUAL_MAX_SEQ=4096`, `--max-seq-len 4096`, and 8 generated tokens:

- task: `task_20260713_011742_110310022495`
- exit code: `0`
- TTFT: `8.745s`
- decode: `0.407s` over 7 steps
- TPOT: `58.1 ms/token`
- output: normal Chinese continuation
- no OOM or runtime error

This validates that the full production-shape scratch allocation fits and completes prefill plus decode on the tested A2/A3 device.

## Risk / Compatibility

- This only affects `decode_layer_a8w8.py`.
- BF16 Qwen3-14B is not touched.
- A8W8 prefill is not touched.
- The attention math is unchanged; this is a scheduling / work partitioning change.
- The main risk is device/runtime sensitivity from finer FA task granularity. The ablation was therefore run on the same device for the TPOT comparison.

## Related Work

- Builds on the Qwen3-14B A8W8 bring-up and fused decode path.
- Complements serving-side L3 dispatch work in `pypto-serving`; this PR is the kernel-side decode attention scheduling optimization.
- Tracking issue: #665

title: Update: cube-tile-tuning b_trans layout, DMA waste, soft L0C wall
body:
## Summary

Sharpens the `cube-tile-tuning` skill after using it to tune the DSv4 routed-expert MoE GEMMs, where three of its assumptions turned out to mislead.

**`hint_l1_tile.py`**

- **Add `--b-trans`** — model the weight as K-contiguous (`B=[N,K]`, the layout LLM weight matmuls actually use, and the one `tile_budget.py` already assumed). B's DMA row becomes `TK*bb`, so a sub-cache-line K tile correctly shows up as a wasted 512 B line and a doubled B load. Previously the tool only modelled a plain row-major `B=[K,N]`, so it happily suggested a sub-cache-line TK — the exact trap the skill doc warns about. Default is unchanged for backward compatibility.
- **Report MAC waste and DMA waste** instead of one blended `waste` column. DMA waste (bytes moved vs. the same tiling costed with real dims and no line rounding) is the bandwidth-honest number, and unlike MAC waste it is per-operand: padding M inflates A and C but never B. For a weight-dominated decode GEMM (tiny M, huge B), MAC waste reads 100% while DMA waste stays near zero — one number could not express both.
- **Drop the `--max-waste` filter.** Waste is already priced into the DMA cost that ranks candidates, so filtering on it double-counted; worse, for a sub-fragment M (`M < tile_multiple`, where the padding is unavoidable and identical across every candidate) the 25% default pruned *every* feasible tiling and the tool returned nothing.

**`SKILL.md`**

- **Acc (L0C) is a *soft* wall.** pypto's `AutoTileMatmulL0` output-tiles an oversized `[M,N]` fragment rather than failing, at a per-tile FIXPIPE L0C→L1 drain (~245 cycles on 910B, fully exposed — no L0C double-buffer emitter yet). So size M/N to L0C to *avoid drains*, not because bigger fails. The hard walls are Mat (L1) and UB. Notes where auto-tiling is deferred (`matmul_acc`, Vec/PV left operand, mixed on-chip consumer), which is when Acc goes hard again.
- **Left/Right (L0A/L0B) are compiler-managed, not DSL knobs.** pypto sub-tiles each L1 fragment through L0A/L0B itself, so Right/L0B routinely reads ~100% in the memory report even with L1 to spare — that is pypto saturating its staging buffer, not a wall you set. The old doc invited readers to tune against it ("a near-full Right/Mat means the weight tile is the wall"), which sends you shrinking a tile for no reason. Tune only Mat (L1), Acc (L0C), and Vec (UB).

Ports the small sparse-kernel piece of CSA's #734 refactor to the HCA & SWA decode paths: collapse `rope_cs` from a 2-task spmd fan-out into a single `pl.at`, matching what #734 did in CSA's `decode_sparse_attn.py`. Structural parity only — bit-exact, wall-neutral.

title: Add: Qwen3 decode attention via CANN FAI (static batch-16)
body:
## What

Replaces the internal fused flash-attention (`fa_fused` / `fa_work_build`) in the
Qwen3-14B decode path with an external CCEC mixed kernel derived from CANN
**FusedInferAttentionScore**, consuming vLLM's active-TND query and **BSND** paged-KV
layouts directly (no materialized reshape) via its own runtime tiler, GM metadata,
and workspace. Decode and prefill both write BSND paged KV. CANN source provenance in `NOTICE`.

## Scope: static batch-16 only

Deliberately keeps the model's **original static decode contract** (`BATCH=16`) rather
than a dynamic active-batch descriptor:
- decode contract args stay `B` (not `USER_BATCH`); `supported_batch_sizes: "16"`
- **no lib-serving contract change, no serving-side batching rework** (pypto-serving needs only a submodule bump, not the active-prefix path)
- the batch-1 flash-decode path is **fully removed** — tiler split-KV branch + helpers (`fill_flash_decode` etc.) and the per-launch core reduction (`is_b1` / `B1_BLOCK_DIM`), ~150 lines. No dormant/dead B1 code remains.

Limited to a2a3.

## Verification (a3)

- Single-layer decode **golden PASS** (`ratio_allclose`, ragged batch)
- B16 attention **~235 µs @ 98% core occupancy** (uniform 3338, 2-layer swimlane) — on par with the internal fa baseline (~233 µs) and vLLM FIA device (~233 µs)

title: [Feature] Make DeepSeek V4 pypto-lib packed prefill operators use dynamic token shapes
body:
Related: #410

## Summary

Make the DeepSeek V4 `pypto-lib` packed prefill operator path use a dynamic logical token dimension throughout `prefill_fwd`, Attention, and MoE instead of passing fixed-`T` tensors together with a runtime `num_tokens` scalar that marks only a valid prefix.

`prefill_layer_core` is an initial dynamic-shape experiment: it accepts packed dynamic inputs, loops over requests and fixed-`T` tiles, creates tile-local `[T, ...]` views, and passes `valid_n` as `num_tokens` to the existing fixed-shape Attention and MoE children. This makes the orchestration layer dynamic, but the leaf operators still allocate and schedule for `T` and use `num_tokens` to mask padded rows.

The desired contract is that the logical token count comes from the dynamic leading dimension of the input tensors. Request boundaries remain explicit metadata, but `num_tokens` should no longer be a runtime kernel argument used to describe the valid prefix of a fixed-size tensor.

This issue is narrower than #410. Issue #410 covers broad DeepSeek V4 B/S, KV-cache, and block-table dynamic-shape refactoring. This issue tracks the missing packed-prefill contract across the full token path, including Gate/MoE, Attention composition, `prefill_fwd`, and removal of the redundant `num_tokens` runtime parameter.

## Motivation / Use Case

The current implementation has two competing sources of truth for token count:

- the physical tensor shape, which is fixed to `T`; and
- `num_tokens`, which tells each child how many leading rows are logically valid.

This causes several problems:

- `prefill_layer_core` must loop over requests and fixed-size tiles primarily to satisfy fixed-shape child APIs;
- partial tiles allocate and propagate padded `[T, ...]` intermediates;
- Attention, Gate, dispatch/combine, and MoE contain repeated `t < num_tokens` or `active_tokens` guards;
- the public `prefill_fwd` signature remains fixed-shape even though several lower-level primitives already support a dynamic token dimension;
- callers must keep tensor shapes and `num_tokens` consistent manually.

A single compiled prefill graph should accept different packed token counts, including non-tile-aligned lengths, while preserving request isolation, cache updates, sparse-attention semantics, and EP MoE behavior.

## Current Behavior

The current packed-layer experiment behaves as follows:

```text
dynamic packed token buffer
  -> loop over requests
  -> split each request into fixed-T tiles
  -> create [T, ...] child tensors with valid_shape=[valid_tok, ...]
  -> call fixed-T Attention with num_tokens=valid_tok
  -> call fixed-T MoE with num_tokens=valid_tok
  -> scatter the full tile back into the packed output
```

Relevant code paths include:

- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_layer.py::prefill_layer_core`
- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_fwd.py::prefill_fwd`
- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_attention_{swa,hca,csa}.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_sparse_attn.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_compressor_ratio{4,128}.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_indexer.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_indexer_compressor.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4/gate.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4/moe.py`

Some shared primitives already demonstrate the intended dynamic-token pattern, including `hc_pre.py`, `hc_post.py`, `rmsnorm.py`, and `qkv_proj_rope.py`, but their fixed-shape callers currently recreate `[T, ...]` intermediates.

## pypto-lib Operator Flow

```text
packed tokens [TOKENS_DYN, ...]
  + request boundaries / positions / slot mappings
  -> dynamic-token Attention path
       -> HC pre / RMSNorm / QKV + RoPE
       -> compressor / indexer / sparse attention as required by SWA, HCA, or CSA
       -> HC post
  -> dynamic-token Gate and EP MoE
       -> routing / dispatch / experts / combine
  -> next layer
  -> final HC head / norm / LM head
  -> packed output [TOKENS_DYN, ...]
```

The leading dynamic dimension is the source of truth for total logical tokens. Multi-request boundaries must still be carried by explicit metadata such as `chunk_offsets` or cumulative request offsets; removing `num_tokens` does not mean removing request-boundary metadata.

## Repository / Layer Responsibilities

- `pypto-lib/models/deepseek/v4`: own the dynamic token-shape contracts, leaf-kernel conversions, packed Attention/MoE composition, golden tests, and `prefill_fwd` integration covered by this issue.
- `pypto`: provide the existing `pl.dynamic`, `bind_dynamic`, `pl.tensor.dim`, dynamic slicing/reshape, and distributed compilation support. Any missing compiler capability discovered during implementation should be reported separately rather than silently expanding this issue.
- `pypto-serving`: eventually pass packed inputs and request-boundary metadata to the new kernel contract. Serving-runner or scheduler changes are not part of this issue.

## Proposed API / Behavior

Use a dynamic token symbol in token-major kernel signatures and bind it at JIT entry points:

```python
TOKENS_DYN = pl.dynamic("DEEPSEEK_PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN")

@pl.jit
def prefill_component(
    x: pl.Tensor[[TOKENS_DYN, D], pl.BF16],
    y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[TOKENS_DYN, D], pl.BF16]],
    ...,
):
    x.bind_dynamic(0, TOKENS_DYN)
    y.bind_dynamic(0, TOKENS_DYN)
    token_count = pl.tensor.dim(x, 0)
    ...
```

For the runtime kernel contract:

- remove `num_tokens: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32]` from prefill leaf APIs and from `prefill_fwd`;
- derive the token extent from the dynamic tensor dimension;
- propagate the same dynamic token symbol to outputs and token-aligned metadata;
- use explicit offsets/length metadata for request segmentation, not a fixed physical `T` plus valid-prefix scalar;
- allow static internal tile sizes and bounded internal padding where required for code generation or hardware efficiency, but do not expose that padding as the logical tensor shape or require the caller to provide `num_tokens`;
- host-side fixture builders may still accept an integer token count to generate test data, but it must not be part of the compiled kernel API.

## Incremental Implementation Plan

Convert and validate small modules one at a time, in dependency order. Each step should remain independently reviewable.

### Phase 1: Establish the token-shape contract

- Define or reuse one DeepSeek V4 prefill dynamic token symbol.
- Add reusable tests that compile once and run multiple logical token lengths.
- Verify the already-dynamic primitives (`hc_pre`, `hc_post`, `rmsnorm`, `qkv_proj_rope`, `hc_head`, and `lm_head`) compose without reintroducing fixed `[T, ...]` intermediates.
- Document the distinction between total token extent and per-request boundaries.

### First PR / First Step: Dynamic Gate

Start with `models/deepseek/v4/gate.py::gate`, the smallest remaining independently verifiable prefill component that directly consumes `num_tokens`:

- give `x_mixed`, `input_ids`, `x_norm`, quantization outputs, routing indices, and routing weights the same dynamic leading token dimension;
- derive the logical token count from `pl.tensor.dim(x_mixed, 0)`;
- remove the runtime `num_tokens` argument from the compiled Gate API and its caller-facing test entry point;
- retain static internal tile sizes and aligned temporary buffers where required, while masking only internal alignment padding;
- compile once and validate multiple token lengths, including one non-tile-aligned length and the existing `T` length.

This first PR does not need to convert distributed MoE or Attention. After the Gate contract is validated, continue through `moe`, then the Attention leaf dependencies and compositions described below.

### Phase 2: Dynamic Gate and MoE

- Convert `gate` so the token extent comes from its input shape.
- Convert routing, dispatch, expert, and combine buffers/loops to dynamic logical tokens while preserving static hardware tiling where needed.
- Convert `moe` and its output to the same dynamic token dimension.
- Remove the prefill-path `num_tokens` argument from Gate/MoE calls.
- Validate EP2 routing, empty/padded routing slots, and non-tile-aligned token counts.

### Phase 3: Dynamic Attention leaf modules

- Convert `prefill_compressor_ratio128`.
- Convert `prefill_compressor_ratio4`.
- Convert `prefill_indexer_compressor` and `prefill_indexer`.
- Convert `prefill_sparse_attn`.
- Ensure token-aligned position IDs, slot mappings, sparse indices, and outputs share the dynamic leading dimension.
- Keep cache and block-table dynamic-dimension work aligned with #410 rather than duplicating its ownership.

### Phase 4: Dynamic Attention compositions

- Convert `prefill_attention_swa` first as the smallest composition.
- Convert `prefill_attention_hca` after ratio-128 compression is dynamic.
- Convert `prefill_attention_csa` after ratio-4 compression, indexer, and sparse attention are dynamic.
- Remove `num_tokens` from all three Attention APIs.
- Preserve per-request causal/cache isolation through explicit packed-request metadata.

### Phase 5: Integrate packed layer and full forward

- Update `prefill_layer_core` so it no longer creates fixed `[T, ...]` child tensors solely to satisfy fixed-shape children.
- Remove fixed-tile valid-prefix plumbing (`valid_n`) from child calls.
- Update `prefill_fwd` inputs, intermediates, outputs, and host wrapper to carry the dynamic token dimension throughout the `pypto-lib` operator path.
- Remove the runtime `num_tokens` argument from `prefill_fwd` and `l3_prefill_fwd`.
- Retain internal tiling only as an implementation detail, not as the public logical-shape contract.

## Current Scope

- Dynamic logical token dimension for the DeepSeek V4 packed prefill path in `pypto-lib`.
- Incremental conversion of the prefill Attention and MoE dependency chains.
- Removal of `num_tokens` from compiled prefill kernel APIs.
- Request-aware packed metadata contract.
- Golden, compile, and multi-shape validation for the converted modules and full `prefill_fwd`.

## Out of Scope

- Decode-path `num_tokens` cleanup.
- Changing model-static dimensions such as `D`, head dimensions, expert counts, or layer count.
- Replacing static hardware tiling constants with dynamic values.
- General KV-cache and block-table dynamic-shape ownership already tracked by #410, except compatibility changes required by the prefill token path.
- `pypto-serving` scheduler, batching policy, or runner integration.
- New PyPTO compiler features; blockers should be filed as separate `pypto` issues.
- Introducing code, dependencies, or API coupling from external inference repositories; the implementation must use existing PyPTO and PyPTO-Lib abstractions.
- Performance parity work beyond preventing obvious padded-prefix computation; performance tuning can follow functional support.

## Alternatives Considered

### Keep fixed `[T, ...]` tensors and pass `num_tokens`

This is the current design. It avoids dynamic leaf shapes but duplicates token-count state, requires prefix guards, and keeps padded intermediates throughout the graph.

### Make only `prefill_layer_core` dynamic

This is the current experiment. It proves dynamic packed inputs can be accepted, but it pushes request/tile loops and padding into the orchestration layer while leaving the actual Attention and MoE contracts static.

### Recompile for every token count

This avoids runtime dynamic shapes but defeats the goal of reusing one compiled prefill graph across varying request batches and chunk sizes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single compiled converted component can run at least three token lengths, including a non-tile-aligned length, without recompilation.
- [ ] `gate` and `moe` use a dynamic leading token dimension and do not accept a runtime prefill `num_tokens` argument.
- [ ] `prefill_attention_swa`, `prefill_attention_hca`, and `prefill_attention_csa` use a dynamic leading token dimension and do not accept `num_tokens`.
- [ ] Their required leaf modules?compressors, indexer/indexer-compressor, and sparse attention?support the same dynamic logical token extent.
- [ ] `prefill_fwd` and its host wrapper no longer expose `num_tokens`; outputs and token-aligned metadata derive their logical extent from input shapes.
- [ ] Packed multi-request execution preserves request boundaries, causal behavior, slot mappings, cache/state updates, and MoE routing isolation.
- [ ] Golden comparisons cover single request, multiple requests, full-tile, and partial/non-tile-aligned token lengths.
- [ ] EP2 compile/device validation passes for the full packed prefill path.
- [ ] No fixed `[T, ...]` padded child tensor is required solely to communicate a shorter valid prefix. Internal hardware-alignment padding remains allowed as an implementation detail.
- [ ] Existing fixed-shape behavior remains numerically compatible for `token_count == T`.

## Additional Context

- Related issue: #410 (`DeepSeek-V4 Dynamic Shape Refactoring & Code Reuse`)
- Existing experiment: `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_layer.py::prefill_layer_core`
- Full forward target: `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_fwd.py::prefill_fwd`

title: PoC: fold dsv4/moe dispatch/combine wait into syncall barriers
body:
> **Draft / PoC — not ready to merge.** Opened to document the approach and its measured trade-offs. See "Status" below.

## Summary

Experiment: remove the `dispatch_wait` and `combine_wait` runtime tasks in
`dsv4/moe` by folding their cross-rank `notify`/`wait` into the neighbouring SPMD
launch, using a full-occupancy hard (FFTS) `pl.system.syncall` to rendezvous the
blocks instead of a separate task boundary. Also merges `dispatch_push` +
`dispatch_gather` into a single `dispatch_exchange` task, removing the
`push -> gather` boundary and its scheduling gaps.

**Mechanism (why the fold is correct):** every cross-rank `TPUT` self-drains —
codegen emits a `PIPE_ALL` barrier after each put (`pto_ops_distributed.cpp`) —
so once a barrier rendezvouses all blocks, every outgoing put has landed and
block 0 can `notify` peers without racing the data. No separate landing fence is
needed; the former `pl.at(...wait...)` task only existed to provide that
cross-block rendezvous, which the barrier now supplies.

Structural result: dispatch `meta + push + wait + gather` (4 tasks) → `meta +
exchange` (2 tasks); combine `scatter + wait + reduce` (3) → `scatter + reduce`
(2). The `wait` tasks and the `push -> gather` scheduling gaps are gone.

## Status — NOT ready to merge

Correctness PASSes on `moe.py`'s own golden (fixed input, ep2), and the
scheduling gaps are removed as intended, but the net result does not justify
merging:

- **Perf is wash-to-negative.** Measured on the compute-dominated rank
  (straggler-free), dispatch **end-to-end incl. scheduling gaps: 33.6 µs →
  41.8 µs**. The removed gaps (~4.7 µs) are real, but the full-occupancy
  (48-core) hard barriers + 32→48 block launch cost more than the folded task
  boundaries save. `decode_fwd` overall is unchanged-to-slightly-slower
  (82.5 → 83.0 ms, same-scale run).
- **Intermittent spin.** Observed once on a random-input `moe.py` run (a
  `route_hash`/barrier lane spun ~349 ms). Input-dependent; root cause is the
  full-occupancy barrier's sensitivity to per-rank arrival skew.
- **a2a3-only.** `AIV_CORES = 48` is hardcoded to the a2a3 physical AIV count;
  a5 has a different count and would deadlock (507018). `moe.py` is shared by 6
  forward drivers (decode/prefill × fwd/layer/mtp), so this is a broad blast
  radius.

Added `# ci: no-dep-gen` because the full-occupancy hard `syncall` trips 507018
under dep_gen/DFX (same constraint `hc_pre` already carries, pypto#1931).

## What would make it a real win

A lightweight **partial-occupancy** barrier: keep the fold at `pl.spmd(N_LOCAL)`
(32 blocks, no full-occupancy drain gap / idle chaperones) with a *fast* barrier.
The soft GM-polling `syncall` is partial-occupancy but currently spins ~1.2 s, so
it is not usable today — fixing that (framework side) is the real unlock. With a
cheap partial-occupancy barrier the removed scheduling gaps would turn net
positive.

## Related Issues

None (references pypto#1931 for the dep_gen / hard-syncall constraint).

title: perf(dsv4/hca): widen decode sparse_attn qk_pv dispatch to T*SPARSE_BLOCKS
body:
## Summary

HCA decode `qk_pv` was `pl.spmd(T)` with the sparse-block dimension unrolled *inside* each task, so only `T`(=8) cube / 16 vector lanes were engaged during the ~64us qk_pv window — a2a3 has 24 AIC + 48 AIV, i.e. the long pole was leaving half the cores idle.

Move the block index into the spmd dispatch: `pl.spmd(T * SPARSE_BLOCKS)` with `qk_t = qk_item // SPARSE_BLOCKS`, `qk_sb = qk_item - qk_t * SPARSE_BLOCKS`, dropping the inner `pl.unroll` and dedenting its body. Store offsets (`qk_row = qk_blk_base + qk_sb * H_TILE`) are unchanged, so output is bit-identical.

## Why HCA can do a static split (no CSA-style cursor)

CSA's `qk_pv` needs a `qk_plan` load-balance cursor because its valid-block count varies per token. HCA is deterministic — the window block is always live and the compressed tail is masked by `sparse_bias` — so a plain static `T * SPARSE_BLOCKS` split suffices. No `qk_order`/`valid_block_mask` machinery ported. (Static ceiling is 16 lanes at the demo's `SPARSE_BLOCKS=2`; reaching the full 24 AIC would need the CSA cursor, out of scope here.)

## Validation (a2a3, 3-run mean vs same-session baseline)

- `decode_attention_hca` golden **PASS** — bit-exact (`x_out`, `kv_cache`); `compress_ratio=128` / `SPARSE_BLOCKS=2`.
- `qk_pv_aiv` 64.4 -> 49.8us (**−23%**); core engagement doubled (AIV 16->32, AIC 8->16).
- total wall 395 -> ~378us (**−4%**).

## Scope notes

- HCA-only. SWA can't benefit (`SPARSE_BLOCKS=1`, no block dim to widen). CSA already has the more aggressive 24-lane planned dispatch.
- Single file, +56/-55, bit-exact, no precision risk.

title: fix(qwen3-14b/prefill-tq): support long-context prompts via streaming attention (MAX_SEQ=4096)
body:
# qwen3-14B TurboQuant prefill — long-context fix (MAX_SEQ=4096)

- **Commit:** `613c80a`
- **File:** `models/qwen3/14b/qwen3_14b_prefill_tq_draft.py`
- **Date:** 2026-07-22

## Problem

The draft prefill hardcoded `MAX_SEQ = 128`, sizing `rope_cos`/`rope_sin` to
`[128, HEAD_DIM]`. Attention reads `rope_cos[pos]` for `pos` up to `seq_len`, so
prompts >128 tokens read out-of-bounds rope values (clamped on device — no fault,
request still "succeeds") → wrong RoPE → garbage logits. Serving showed correct
output for prompts ≤128 tokens and pure garbage above the ~128 cutoff.

## Fix

- **`MAX_SEQ`: 128 → `M.max_seq` (4096).** Rope tables now cover the full prompt
  length. (This is the core fix for the long-input garbage.)
- **Attention rewritten to chunk-streaming**, mirroring `prefill_fwd_a8w8.py`
  (its lines 433-540): one `for sb0 in range(0, ctx_blocks, SB_BATCH)` chunk loop
  with per-chunk `[SB_BATCH*...]` scratch allocated *inside* the loop (liveness
  scoped per chunk), replacing `[MAX_CTX_BLOCKS*...]` buffers kept live across
  four separate full-range loops. Scratch is now sized by the constant `SB_BATCH`,
  independent of prompt length (no short-prompt padding to a worst-case tile).
- **`SB_BATCH`: 128 → 32** (matches `prefill_fwd_a8w8`).
- Causal `valid_shape` + `fillpad(min)` masking preserved per lane.
- Removed dead `MAX_CTX_BLOCKS` constant.

Note: this prefill uses **dequant-attention** — it reads dequantized K/V from the
quantized cache (gather → renorm → unrotate → rescale), like decode; there is no
FP K/V path. (The older walkthrough note saying "prefill reads FP K/V" is stale.)

## Verification (device a2a3)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| prefill golden `--max-seq 4096` | **PASS** (ctx_blocks=32) |
| decode golden `--max-seq 4096` | **PASS** (decode unchanged; re-verified) |
| full-model (40-layer) `npu_generate`, 1500-token prompt + TQ | **completes** (prefill ~26s, decode ~620ms/step) |
| single-batch serving, 1509-token prompt | **completes** (~30s) |

## Known separate issues (NOT fixed by this change)

These are independent of the MAX_SEQ fix and remain open:

- **Serving multi-batch / 2nd sequential request → `HEAP_RING_DEADLOCK`** (507018).
  A single ~1500-token TQ prefill emits ~44k tasks / ~2GB heap; the pypto runtime
  does not fully clear the ring heap between runs (`reset_for_reuse` zeroes the
  cursor but not the device-side `heap_used`), so the 2nd request sees the heap
  full and deadlocks. Invariant across `SBATCH` / `PTO2_RING_TASK_WINDOW` /
  `PTO2_RING_HEAP`. **Single short-batch serving works.** Root cause is in the
  pypto runtime, not this kernel. Diagnostic: `~/ascend/log/debug/device-*/*.log`,
  grep `TaskAllocator.*BLOCKED` (look at `tasks` vs `heap_used`).
- **TQ decode is slow** (~620ms/step at long context; ~1.4-1.8 tok/s). The TQ
  decode lacks the `fa_fused` optimization the FP decode has, and does a heavy
  per-step full-KV gather-dequant. Decode kernel unchanged here. ms/step scales
  with context (O(context) dequant), so long generation is slow.
- **scale 1/16 KV-scale bug** (~14% precision at short context).
  `turboquant_kv.py` Scope A/C write the per-token scale with a bare `pl.range`
  reassign (no `init_values`/`yield_`) → only 1/16 scales survive. Still open.

title: perf(dsv4): refine CSA projection, SWA merge, and decode sparse-K gathers
body:
## Summary
- Pipeline CSA decode proj_a, per-group quantization, and balanced proj_b blocks to avoid serializing grouped output projection.
- Add CSA profiling replay options and align the HC-pre Golden reduction tree with the kernel execution order.
- Restore SWA merge_norm to one 32-block AIV grid while retaining fused inverse RoPE and contiguous per-group stores.
- Hoist the HCA decode sparse-K gather out of `qk_pv` into its own spmd grid, with bulk-run window copies and window/compressed interleaving so the gather stays off `qk_pv`'s critical path.
- Bulk-copy the contiguous window runs in the SWA decode gather too.

## Current decode performance

`hc_post` end, us. a2a3, `--start-pos 8192`, `--enable-l2-swimlane 1`.

| path | pypto (3 runs) | median | ASC |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| CSA | 423.2 / 423.0 / 428.5 | 423.2 | 465 |
| HCA | 313.0 / 307.4 / 306.8 | 307.4 | 307 |
| SWA | 291.1 / 284.3 / 291.9 | 291.1 | 280 |
| MoE | 521.9 / 514.5 / 499.3 | 514.5 | 479 |

CSA is the most expensive attention path in absolute terms, for two reasons visible in the swimlane:

- Its `qk_pv` exec is 44.5-47.7us (24 aic + 48 aiv blocks) vs 9-14us for HCA, and it still gathers inside `qk_pv` — the transformation applied to HCA/SWA here has not been ported to it.
- The indexer chain (`idx_qr_proj` -> `qr_rope` -> `qr_hadamard` -> `score_mat` -> `score_reduce` -> `topk` -> `csa_slots_build_valid_qk_plan`) runs serially to ~222us before `qk_pv` can start at ~232us.

## Decode sparse-K gather

Both HCA and SWA ran the sparse-K gather as a per-row loop: a scalar index read plus a 1KB row DMA. That is issue-overhead bound (~0.44us/row, ~2.3 GB/s effective), not bandwidth bound.

A decode window is a run of consecutive logical positions, so a 16-row sub-tile whose first/last slots are 15 apart lives in one paged block and moves in ONE bulk DMA. Only a block-straddling or `-1` sub-tile falls back to the per-row copy (~0.02us/row bulk vs ~0.44us/row).

### HCA: gather hoisted out of `qk_pv`

`qk_pv` ran a 128-iteration scalar-read + `gather_row` loop before its cube work, costing ~23us of its ~33us exec. It now loads a plain `[ATTN_K_TILE, HEAD_DIM]` slice from a contiguous GM buffer filled by a separate grid (same shape as `decode_sparse_attn_swa`).

Hoisting alone is a regression — the GM round-trip doubles the per-row cost (180ns -> 356ns) and the gather's straggler then gates `qk_pv`. Two choices keep it off the critical path:

- **Bulk window runs**, as above.
- **Interleaved segments, grid pinned to 32.** Each block carries a quarter of the window AND a quarter of the compressed tail. Splitting the two into separate tasks makes the scattered per-row topk rows the straggler; and the grid stays at `T*4 = 32` blocks so it co-resides with the 16 `qproj_dequant` blocks in one AIV wave.

Gather now ends before the Q chain does, so `qk_pv` still starts at ~150us while its exec drops 32.6 -> 9-14us.

### SWA: bulk runs only

`swa_gather_kv` exec 17.6 -> 6.1us (-65%), total core work 4268 -> 3810us (-11%). `hc_post` end is unchanged: SWA's gather already finished ~25us before `qk_pv` could start, because `qk_pv` waits on the Q chain. The saving lands off the critical path and only frees AIV occupancy for co-resident scopes.

## Validation
- `decode_attention_hca` at `--start-pos 8192` and at the default per-batch start positions (which exercise the block-straddling and `-1` per-row fallbacks): `kv_cache` and `x_out` PASS.
- `decode_sparse_attn_hca` standalone harness: `attn_out` PASS.
- `decode_attention_swa` at `--start-pos 8192`: `kv_cache` and `x_out` PASS.

title: CI: fix orphaned-task cleanup and raise task-submit timeouts
body:
## Summary

Two CI fixes around `task-submit` lifetime management.

**1. `kill-orphaned-tasks` never actually killed anything.** The action piped `task-submit --list` into a grep for the job's full checkout path. `--list` is a human-facing view that truncates the command column to 77 chars, so the full path never appeared in the output and the grep never matched — the cleanup step has been silently killing nothing. Tasks from cancelled jobs kept running server-side and held a shared card until `--max-time` bounded them.

- Match with `task-submit --find` instead: it greps the untruncated `COMMAND` and prints bare task-ids. This requires an up-to-date `task-submit` on the runner.
- Fail loudly if `--find` errors, rather than `|| true`-ing the whole pipeline back into a silent no-op.
- Print a kill count, so a broken cleanup step is distinguishable from a cleanup step that had nothing to do.

**2. Device cases were being rejected at submit time** when they queued behind a busy card pool for longer than `task-submit` was willing to wait.

- Raise every `task-submit --timeout` to 3600 (`ci.yml`, `daily_ci.yml`, and the `pypto-serving-tests` action, which was at 1200). `--max-time` is unchanged.
- Lift the job `timeout-minutes` so a job outlives a single `task-submit`'s worst case — otherwise GitHub kills the job before `task-submit`'s own timeout can fire, and the first queued case eats the entire job budget: `a2a3` 60 → 120, daily `model-tests-a2a3` 60 → 120, `serving` 90 → 180 (serving runs the qwen3 and deepseek submits back to back, so it worst-cases at 2 × (3600 + 1800)).

## Related Issues

N/A

title: exp(dsv4/moe): fold dispatch notify into push + early-dispatch overlap
body:
> **Draft / experiment — not for merge.** Opened to document the approach and its measured behaviour on device.

## Summary

Dispatch-side scheduling experiment on `dsv4/moe` (device a2a3 ep2, **7/7 golden PASS**):

- **Fold the `data_arrived` notify into `dispatch_push`.** Each of the `N_LOCAL` push blocks signals every peer once after its own puts — a counting barrier where the peer waits `N_LOCAL * moe_epoch`. `dispatch_wait` becomes wait-only and depends on `dispatch_meta` instead of `dispatch_push`, so it can spin on peers' `data_arrived` counters while the local push is still running.
- **`allow_early_resolve=True` on `dispatch_meta` / `dispatch_wait`** so the scheduler pre-stages the wait onto an idle core. Confirmed on the level-4 swimlane: `dispatch_wait` now overlaps push (starts ~6us vs ~16us before).

### Measured findings

- **wait overlap works**: with early-dispatch the wait-only task is pre-staged onto one of the ~11 idle AIV cores during push (push uses 32/48), starting before push ends. Changing the dependency edge alone (meta vs push) was *not* enough — early-dispatch is the mechanism that actually stages it.
- **`dispatch_gather` stays late** (~44us, ~27us after its deps resolve at ~10us) even though AIV cores are fully idle after push. Root cause per level-4 AICPU lane: the scheduler is serialized in an 18us `complete(19)` batch draining push's 32 block completions, and does not dispatch during it — a scheduler-throughput gate, not cores or deps.
- **Net dispatch-segment latency at ep2 is a wash** — inter-rank meta-barrier skew (µs–ms) dominates the few-µs scheduling deltas.

### Caveat

`recv_x` rides a self-draining TPUT, but `recv_aux` / `recv_route` ride a non-draining `remote_store` (TSTORE), and a `PIPE_ALL` barrier is not a cross-rank DDR fence (PTOAS#872). The in-push notify can in principle race on aux/route visibility; device ep2 was 7/7 PASS, but this is why it stays an experiment.

## Related Issues

None (references pto-isa#197 for the soft-syncall spin and PTOAS#872 for the missing cross-rank DDR fence in TNOTIFY).

title: [Feature] Support device-resident DeepSeek V4 cache pools across prefill and decode
body:
### Summary

Add a DeepSeek V4 serving cache implementation in which prefill and decode share the same persistent, per-rank device-resident cache pools. Serving should not need to pass full cache tensors as shared-host inputs or copy a prefill snapshot into a separate decode cache layout.

This issue is specifically about the physical cache residency and lifecycle needed by serving. The generic serving-contract API remains tracked by #752, while cache metadata and slot/index semantics were discussed in #511, #710, #712, and #735.

### Motivation / Use Case

`pypto-serving` is adapting DeepSeek V4 to DP8 + EP8 on eight NPUs. The current target is one local prefill request per DP rank, which permits up to eight global prefill requests, followed by continuous multi-step decode.

The current DeepSeek integration has to maintain two cache representations:

- fixed-shape shared-host scratch tensors for `l3_prefill_fwd`;
- separate shared-host work-cache tensors for `l3_decode_fwd`;
- a host-side snapshot/copy between the two after prefill.

This is both expensive and incomplete as a serving contract:

- raw shared-host tensors are treated as per-dispatch I/O rather than worker-resident buffers;
- in the generated prefill host program, only the original `kv_cache` is a top-level `InOut` argument, while compressed KV, index/scale caches, and compressor states are top-level inputs. Their device-side mutations therefore cannot be relied on to return through the host fallback;
- resetting the prefill scratch tensors for every invocation loses cache/state from an earlier chunk, so prompts longer than one packed prefill chunk cannot be handled correctly by host snapshotting;
- the handoff must keep all heterogeneous DeepSeek cache families synchronized, including `idx_kv_scale`.

The model architecture requires several cache families, but separate host-backed prefill/decode caches and the snapshot handoff are implementation limitations, not an intrinsic model requirement. The pypto-lib golden runners already describe these caches as `resident="stacked"`; serving needs that resident lifecycle to be exposed and supported by the model implementation.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Please add a DeepSeek V4 cache contract/adapter with the following behavior:

1. Expose a model-owned cache layout descriptor derived from the model constants, covering per-rank shapes, dtypes, capacities, and the complete set of cache pools:
   - original KV cache;
   - compressed KV cache;
   - index KV cache and index scale cache;
   - HCA compressor state;
   - CSA compressor state;
   - CSA inner-compressor state.
2. Allocate/upload those pools once as worker-resident `StackedDeviceTensor` (or an equivalent persistent device handle) after the distributed workers are prepared.
3. Let both `l3_prefill_fwd` and `l3_decode_fwd` consume the same per-rank persistent pool handles. Prefer having prefill write the final decode cache layout directly using scheduler-provided block tables/slot mappings.
4. If the packed prefill and decode layouts cannot initially be unified, provide an explicit device-side conversion/copy operation. A host round trip should not be required.
5. Preserve cache and compressor state across repeated/chunked prefill dispatches; a suffix chunk must be able to read all prior chunks for the same request.
6. Define ownership and lifecycle clearly: allocate once per worker/model, reuse across prefill and decode dispatches, release request block metadata on completion, and free the pools when the worker/model closes.
7. Keep one local prefill request per DP rank as an acceptable first stage, while allowing DP8 to prefill eight global requests concurrently. The contract should not hard-code global batch size 1.
8. If a shared-host fallback remains supported, mark every mutated cache/state argument as output-capable and validate that no state is silently discarded. The resident path should be the normal serving path.

The model-owned adapter should be consumable by the generic serving contract proposed in #752 so `pypto-serving` does not duplicate DeepSeek-specific shapes or ABI details.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Prefill and decode use the same persistent per-rank device cache pools, or use an explicit device-side handoff with no full-cache D2H/H2D round trip.
- All cache families and compressor states survive across dispatches, including `idx_kv_scale`.
- A short prompt followed by multiple decode steps matches the reference output.
- A prompt spanning multiple packed prefill chunks (at least longer than 128 tokens) matches the reference output.
- Tests cross both compressed-cache update boundaries (ratio 4 and ratio 128) so correctness is not validated only by short prompts.
- Two or more requests placed on different DP ranks can prefill and decode without overwriting each other's cache state; DP8 can accept up to eight simultaneous local-batch-1 prefills.
- Cache blocks/state are correctly reclaimed when requests finish, and repeated requests do not observe stale data.
- Existing standalone/golden DeepSeek V4 tests continue to pass.

### Alternatives Considered

1. **Host snapshot from prefill scratch into decode cache (current serving workaround):** rejected as the final design because it introduces large transfers, can discard input-only device mutations, and does not preserve earlier prefill chunks.
2. **Separate resident prefill and decode pools plus device-side conversion:** acceptable as a transitional implementation, but it uses more device memory than sharing one layout.
3. **Mark every shared-host cache tensor as `InOut`:** useful for a correctness fallback, but copying all DeepSeek cache/state tensors on every dispatch is not suitable for serving performance.

### Additional Context

Related issues:

- #752: generic pypto-lib serving contract
- #511: DeepSeek V4 KV-cache metadata/serving contract
- #710 and #712: decode/prefill SWA physical-slot contracts
- #735: cache-first paged prefill sparse-attention API
- #766: dynamic token shapes for packed prefill operators
- hw-native-sys/pypto-serving#42: DeepSeek KV-cache serving integration

Relevant model sources include `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_fwd.py` and `models/deepseek/v4/decode_fwd.py`, where the golden runner cache specifications are already marked as stacked resident tensors.

title: fix(dsv4): keep prefill_layer x_hc/position_ids full-[T] for T_DYN children
body:
## Summary
- pypto now intersects valid regions across function calls and rejects binding a dynamic type variable to two different extents. `prefill_layer_core` sliced `x_hc_tile` / `position_ids_tile` with `valid_shape=[valid_tok]`, but these feed `T_DYN`-parameterized children (`hc_pre`, `hc_post`, `materialize_rope_rows`) whose sibling tensors are full-`[T]`, so `T_DYN` was bound to both `valid_tok` and `T` — a compile error (`Dynamic type variable 'T_DYN' has conflicting bindings 128 and valid_tok`).
- Pass `x_hc` / `position_ids` as full-`[T]` slices; `num_tokens` already gates the padded tail (this matches the decode path, fixed `T`). Slot/index mappings keep their `valid_shape` — they reach only fixed-`[T]` params (no `T_DYN` bind) and the narrowing keeps padded `-1` slots out of the KV/state cache scatters.

title: perf(dsv4/moe): overlap dispatch payload-arrival wait with push
body:
## Summary

Restructure the **dispatch** handshake in `dsv4/moe` so the payload-arrival wait can overlap the bulk transfer instead of being serialized after it. The combine path is intentionally left unchanged.

### Dispatch

- **Fold the `data_arrived` notify into `dispatch_push`.** Each of the `N_LOCAL` push blocks signals every peer once after its own puts, and the peer waits for `N_LOCAL * moe_epoch`.
- **Make `dispatch_wait` wait-only.** It depends on `dispatch_meta` rather than `dispatch_push` and uses `allow_early_resolve=True`, allowing it to spin on peer counters while the local push is still running.
- **Add an explicit `_push_tid` dependency to `dispatch_gather`.** This preserves ordering for this rank's local `dst == my_rank` puts after the wait is detached from the push.

## Correctness note

`recv_aux` and `recv_route` use non-draining `remote_store` operations (cf. PTOAS#872). The counting barrier gates the gather on notifications that each block increments only after issuing its own puts in program order.

## Validation

- Local pre-commit suite: PASS
- Device a2a3, ep2: `moe.py` golden `x_next` PASS with ptoas 0.48

title: perf(dsv4 gate): defer RMSNorm, fp32-native quant, per-row ffn_norm, vectorized route (~40->33us)
body:
## Summary
Optimize the DeepSeek-V4 MoE gate router front so the in-pipeline gate window (ffn_norm start -> route_hash end, balanced EP2) drops **~40us -> ~33us**. The gate matmul stays **fp32 x fp32** to match the asc A2/A3 reference (a2a3 gate_w is fp32; only ASCEND_950 uses bf16 + `16cast32`).

- **Defer the per-token inv_rms scalar** (qwen3 / qkv_proj_rope style): store `xg = x*gamma` and apply `inv_rms` late — a `[16,1]` row-scale on the gate logits, and (since symmetric per-token int8 quant is invariant to a positive scalar) only on `x_norm_scale`. `sq_sum` and `xg` share ONE pass over `x_mixed`.
- **fp32-native quant**: `xg_buf` stays fp32 end to end (no bf16 round-trip), matching `qkv_proj_rope`; the gate matmul reads it directly. Drops the dead `x_norm` (bf16) output.
- **Per-row ffn_norm** (1 token / core, `pl.spmd`): each core loads its token into a physical `[8, FFN_D_TILE]` tile with valid `[1, FFN_D_TILE]`, so the reduction output is physically `[8,1]` (col-major 32B) valid `[1,1]` — a plain `[1,1]` fp32 reduction tile is 4B and fails the ptoas 32B tile floor. ffn_norm 12.6 -> 6.2us (8-way parallel). Mirrors the runtime `row_sum_return` kernel.
- **Vectorized route_hash score gather**: replaced 48 per-eid scalar `route_scores` reads with one batched `pl.gather` + `set_validshape`/`fillpad` (like route_sort). route_hash 9.9 -> 5.2us.
- **allow_early_resolve** on ffn_norm / gate / route_hash / route_sort so the gate head overlaps upstream attention/hc_pre and dispatch pre-stages sooner.

Standalone gate.py PASS on both hash and score-sort routes; moe.py EP2 balanced `x_next` PASS.

title: Make Qwen3 device top-k selection exact
body:
## Summary

Follow up on #769 by replacing the Qwen3-14B per-chunk Top-4 approximation with a provably exact full-vocabulary Top-32 selector.

## What Changed

- Split the 151936 real-vocabulary logits into 74 full 2048-token groups and one 384-token tail group.
- Compute an exact Top-32 for each group with `sort32` and `mrgsort`.
- Merge the resulting `75 x 32 = 2400` candidates in a 4096-entry padded buffer and select the exact global Top-32.
- Keep padded-vocabulary entries excluded with valid-shape masking and minimum-value fill.
- Change the golden implementation to compare directly against `torch.topk(logits[:, :REAL_VOCAB], 32)`.
- Add adversarial fixtures with all Top-32 values concentrated in one 512-token region and distributed across 32 regions.

If an entry is not in its group's Top-32, at least 32 entries in that group rank ahead of it, so it cannot belong to the global Top-32. Therefore the union of exact group Top-32 sets contains the exact global Top-32.

## Validation

- A2/A3 NPU golden comparison: passed for values and token IDs.
- Greedy `selection_k=1` regression: passed.
- Standalone selector, 100 rounds: min 427.1 us, median 427.8 us, mean 428.0 us, max 429.9 us.
- Serving sampling tests after rebase: 29 passed.
- Shared-L3 batch-16 prefill/decode warmup: passed.
- Qwen3-14B 20-token top-k generation: 0.769 s E2E, 26.01 tok/s.

Paired serving PR: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-serving/pull/77

title: perf(dsv4 decode swa): deferred attention RMSNorm and dep cleanup
body:
## Summary

- **Localize decode QKV projection kernels** into `decode_attention_swa` so the SWA decode path is self-contained.
- **Deferred attention RMSNorm (`attn_norm_xgamma`)**: the pre-qkv `inv_rms` is a per-token positive scalar, and `qkv_proj_rope` re-RMSNorms BOTH the qr and kv projections downstream, so `inv_rms` cancels exactly in every qkv output (q / kv / qr int8 / qr_scale). SWA's normalized input feeds only qkv, so `inv_rms` is dropped entirely and just `xg = x*gamma` is stored — removing the sq_sum reduction, the rsqrt, and the whole normalize pass. Being pure elementwise (no reduction), it needs no physical-row tile-floor workaround, so it is parallelized to one token per core with a wide D-tile. The now-unused local `rms_norm` is removed.
  - Not applied to HCA/CSA: there the normalized input also feeds the compressor softmax gate, which is scale-sensitive and needs `inv_rms`.
- **Defer `inv_rms` in `qr_rms_norm_quant`** (same transform as the gate `ffn_norm`): symmetric int8 quant of `qr*gamma` cancels `inv_rms` exactly, so the quant uses `amax(qr*gamma)` directly and `inv_rms` rides only `qr_scale` (dequant). int8 output unchanged.
- **Dependency-chain cleanup** (guided by dep-gen `deps.json`):
  - Drop `allow_early_resolve` from `q_rope_prepare` (not on the qkv critical chain).
  - Remove explicit deps that duplicate tensormap (data) edges, which already order the tasks: `qk_pv deps=[gather_tids[0]]` and `merge_norm deps=[qk_tid, rope_tid]`. `deps.json` confirms only the tensormap edges remain.

Validated on real a2a3 (ptoas 0.48): `x_out` and `kv_cache` PASS. The attention-norm task drops from ~10.8us (`rms_norm`) to ~2.6us (`attn_norm_xgamma`, 1 token/core). At start_pos=8k the hc_post finish is ~281us and stable (10 runs, 276.6-285.1us).

title: fix(dsv4): normalize query before RoPE rotation to fix A5 precision
body:
## Problem

`qkv_proj_rope` rotated the **raw (large-magnitude) dequantized query values before** applying the per-row rmsnorm (rotate-then-normalize). The resulting large intermediates (`raw * cos/sin`, before normalization scales them down) **lost precision on Ascend950 (A5)** and corrupted the query RoPE region.

The kv path already normalizes before rotating and is unaffected (kv output stays correct) — which is also why, in the attention kernels that inline `qkv_proj_rope`, `kv_cache` passed while `x_out` failed.

## Fix

Fold `inv_rms` in **before** the rotation (normalize-then-rotate), matching the kv path.

This is **mathematically equivalent** — `inv_rms` is a per-row scalar, so
`inv_rms*(a*cos+b*sin) == (a*inv_rms)*cos+(b*inv_rms)*sin` — so A2A3 results are unchanged, but the smaller intermediates keep the A5 query RoPE accurate.

## Verification (A5)

`qkv_proj_rope` `q` output: **FAIL (10.8% error, concentrated in the RoPE region) → PASS**. `kv` / `qr` / `qr_scale` unchanged.

## Scope

Fixes the query-RoPE precision divergence in `qkv_proj_rope` on A5. Note: the full attention kernels (`decode/prefill_attention_*`) have **additional**, independent divergences (indexer / sparse-selection paths) that this change does not address — tracked separately.

Removing that boundary, converting MoE, and integrating the full packed `prefill_layer` / `prefill_fwd` path are intentionally deferred to the follow-up PR.

title: feat(qwen3): add --decode-steps for autoregressive decode timing in decode_fwd
body:
## Summary
`decode_fwd.py --validate-fwd` dispatched `decode_fwd` exactly once, so a
STRACE / L2-swimlane timing run only captured a **single** decode invocation —
not a steady-state batch decode.

Add **`--decode-steps N`**: run N autoregressive decode steps. Each step feeds
the previous step's sampled token back as input and **grows the context by one**
(`seq_lens += 1`, `slot_mapping` re-pointed to the new token's KV slot via
`_paged_block_table_slot_mapping`). The sweep starts at `MAX_SEQ - decode_steps`
and ends at `MAX_SEQ`, so the KV pool already sized for `MAX_SEQ`
(`PTO2_MANUAL_MAX_SEQ`) holds the whole run with no overflow (an `assert` guards
`decode_steps < MAX_SEQ`). Host-reference argmax check is skipped for `N > 1`
(perf-only). `N=1` (default) preserves the existing single-step behavior.

## Why
Enables a stable steady-state batch-decode timing sweep from one run, e.g. the
full-model batch-16 × 3338-context decode:
```bash
PTO2_MANUAL_MAX_SEQ=3358 python decode_fwd.py -p a2a3 -d 0 \
  --validate-fwd --fwd-layers 40 --max-seq --decode-steps 20
```
STRACE then reports the median device `Effective` over 20 real growing-context
decode invocations (measured ~37.7 ms/step for batch-16, 40L, ctx 3338→3358).

## Test
- `--decode-steps 20` on a2a3 (batch-16, 40L, ctx 3338→3358): grows without KV
  overflow, 20 STRACE decode invocations, run completes cleanly.
- Default `--decode-steps 1`: unchanged single-step validate path.

title: perf(qwen3-14b decode): fold RoPE into the CANN FAI attention extern

## Summary

- Fold QK-norm and RoPE into the CANN FAI attention extern, removing the
